This game is not like any ordinary game. This game is not anything, like you have ever seen before. Is a game that takes you to a journey of how horror war can be; how much impact each soldier can affect his or her life in an instant. Of how a person feels for the first time ever of what it is to be afraid-this-is hell.
The game was developed by Ubisoft Montpellier, inspired by letters from the Great War. This is a puzzle-adventure game where you played as four fictional characters. The very main character in the middle is Emile, a French farmer who lives in Saulcy-sur-Meurthe from when the war starts he was forced into becoming a French soldier and have to leave his daughter and grandson behind. On the left is Karl, a German farmhand who married Emile’s daughter and have a son, he was also forced to serve in the war but have to move to Germany to become a German soldier. In the far left is Anna an independent woman who is searching for her father and doing service with the French military as a medic. On your right is Freddie, an American soldier who volunteers in the French military for a vengeful purpose.
There was going to be a fifth character to played as George (far right) the British pilot but it was cut off due to the character’s “personality” as humor and the company didn’t want it on a beautifully-sad atmospheric game. So you can only see him in one level of the game. Now I don’t understand why they could have just changed some of the writing to make the character a bit serious, but that is Ubisoft’s problem.
I’m so glad that they set on the First World War and not the usual big 2. I keep seeing the second war topic over and over in games, documents, and museums and I’m tired of it. Now it doesn’t mean I hate hearing more World War 2, I always like learning new information and secrets to the Nazis. Is just that is weird that they don’t put as much of an impact to the Great War as the other. Sure the second war is much worse on the death toll and made a lot of psychological impact on many people that made hard decisions to the world leaders. But you have to remember how it all started the second war and how technology has change drastically in the first war.
How did people react to the Great War? How did soldiers react to the first gas attack in the battle of Ypres. How did the politicians handle the situation? All these are as much important to learn as it is WW2. Maybe because the first war doesn’t have a lot of information due to lack of recording systems at the time, but it’s still can make a great story to it. Yes, you can find documents and videos about WW1 in YouTube or in Google but sometimes for me I can’t understand in some areas of that topic or any fun little facts about them (although sometimes I’m a bit lazy at researching it.)
Since this is a puzzle-adventure game you will be solving some puzzles and I’m glad is not another shooting genre, please no more Call of Duty! Sometimes you will fight some enemies by sneaking at their backside and whack them; you will be accompanying your dog Walt to help you reach hard places and help you on certain puzzles. If it’s too easy for you because of the hint system or highlighted areas just turn them off by turning on Veteran mode.
The story is one of the most beautifully written I have ever played. It focuses a lot on the characters and the situation around the soldiers in the war. Not a single side character is unimportant or poorly use in the game, same goes to the background characters. Each one reacts as a real person would feel; hungry, sad, pain, homesick, and hopeless.
Then when you saw a soldier get shot you feel a little pain for the person to die and have to move on because it is your duty as a soldier to move forth into battle. Even the Germans feels exactly like their enemies are suffering. Is not like in any FPS (First person shooters) that you just shoot some enemies you don’t know of and move on or your comrades that you barely even knew dies and just keep going from point A to B. Hell sometimes you don’t even know who you’re playing as because you’re in first person view!
The background is gorgeous with detail of what’s going on in the battlefield. One minute the land is peaceful the next is smoke clouds, rubble buildings and muddy grounds. In some levels you see on the background corpses everywhere and soldiers screaming in agony! Ubisoft aren’t afraid to show it and they nailed it! The music is also really nice with classical pieces from famous songs, sets the atmosphere flowing.
There are collectables to find such as historical items that tells you fun facts about the war. In each level it tells you in the history facts menu about the war with pictures and documents, all thanks to Apocalypse World War 1 and 14 missions 18 Centenaire, who partnered up with Ubisoft. This is the only game in a long while since I completed a game with 100% all collectables; it was so much fun and interesting to learn new things! I’m not much of a completionist and getting all the historical items only gets you an achievement, but if you like fun facts like me collect them all!
You probably can finish in nine hours and maybe an additional hour or two to collect all the historical items, so that’s eleven hours in total, that is an average good play through. The puzzles are decent, not too challenging but it is a perfect balance. This game gets a 10/10 a masterpiece collection and another perfect example of how games can teach us something and not always violence and corrupt us.
If you can handle the issues it has that’s good, but it is so worth the effort to play, you won’t regretted. I “think” it has less restriction now so I’m glad is less of a hassle. Is also rated T for teen but I think preteens can experience and enjoy the beauty and horror of the Great War. Hope they keep making games like this; it is a breath of fresh air and I hope they make another game like it but in a different war setting.

This game is incredibly compelling. I won't recap "what is Factorio", just my thoughts on why it's good.
The building process is simple enough- there aren't any "secret formulas", technology unlocks as you research it.
You can make your base as complicated as you would like with a robust switching system, but it isn't needed to win the game.
Factorio never punishes you for building the "wrong" thing or placing something in the wrong way. All you need to do is pick it up and move it.
Base defense is important to keep your base working properly- in essence, the aliens create a sort of "wear and tear" on your base that you need to maintain (or automate maintainence of!) which keeps gameplay from getting too "creative sandbox" without taking away freedom to experiment with things.
This game has a lot of self-imposed troubleshooting which is probably my favorite part- figuring out why materials aren't getting to where they need to, or why the throughput isn't what it used to be, or discovering later on that your initial design isn't doing what you wanted it to do, and now you need to find a way to cut it over to a new design without losing total production.

20$ for this? I feel like that price is ripping them off, it's just that good of a game.
My advice:
Schedule your time for playing lol - you might intend to play for an hour but whoops it's 2am
Keep an eye on the subreddit/forum - sometimes I find little resources that help me design stuff
Take your time learning - it might not seem like a fun thing to do but god it is, the sensation of having a working factory is amazing.
Conclusion; have fun and watch the time, it'll slip by easily :)

Well, I spent about 70 good hours on my first run alone. Of course, I was very confused and did not know where everything went or what many of the buildings do. I highly recommend doing a bit of the campaign as I find out they actually try to teach you and give some good tricks and techniques. I recommend to people that you keep your old playthroughs as saves so that you can go back and see your designs. For me, it helped a lot because I can reuse a few old designs but with the randomly generated maps, the game forced me to create new designs. This really sparked a lot of creativity as I start to understand the importantance of placement and planning ahead. Even when it seems like there is are tons of resources nearby, it will run out quick. As you grow your little factory, you will want more productivity which will cause the supply to decrease and demand to increase. You WILL start eating up resources quick and it will only get quicker. It's normal. My current playthrough has about 110hrs invested in it so far, the most of all my save files. My factory right now has thousands of robots flying around alleviating tough decisions and preventing renovatons. Thousands of belts moving around hundreds of thousands products, ores, and plates around. Dozens of trains moving going back and forth, transfering ores and plates from the far edgs of my vision to drop off at my base. There always seems like there is something to do in this game. Whether you have run out of copper ore and will have to liberate some from these alien species surrounding the precious resource you need to keep your factory alive or you have expanded a little too quickly and have surprisingly run out of power. I just can't get tired of playing because there is too much to do to stop. Like, this game is just straight up fun with plenty of room for creativity. This game combines the randomly generated maps of roguelike games and the endless building of Prison Architect. A lot has changed since the first map that I have played and finished. This is still an early access game but it is very well a full game with additional changes and updates every week. I have witness very significant changes to the game. Significant enough that my original designs will not work any more but that just fuels the creativity in me. However way you like to build your base, No other game will make you feel as accomplished as zooming out onto your map and seeing all of your progress from the past hour and thinking "I made this." Your well oiled machine or hot mess will greatly impact your future factories.
Probably my most memorable moment from this game would be inviting my friend to my factory to walk around and learn from my builds. He then found out that grenades were a thing in this game and grabs a ton of them and threw them randomly around at the trees. Just harmless fun until he found out about the cluster grenades and accidently/purposely threw a few around inside my factory.

Very fun and pretty board game. One of the best on Steam.

Armello is a compelling turn-based board game with a variety of different ways to win. There are always 3 opponents (human or AI controlled) along with a variety of NPCs that hinder or help your progress. Being tasked with returning the kingdom to normal, you can choose to defeat the king in combat, become more corrupt than him by being tainted by the 'rot', gather 4 spirit stones to banish him or become the prestige leader and keep the king alive. The different heroes you play as all have their own talents and skills. Each clan has their own rings and coupled with the trinkets and artifacts you uncover during the game you can have a wildly varied hand. At first it seems easy but there are many things out to get you. You have to face perils, survive enemy players and mobs and get close enough to the king to stop him. I love the aesthetics of this game, it certainly feels and sounds like a fantasy adventure you'd want to be a part of. The animal motif fits the theme and the range of cards and effects makes this a deeply complex game. Definitely one of the best board games on Steam.

+ 500 Hours. High time I did a review for ‘Armello.’ Here goes.

Armello is an adventure-strategy board game. Follow four heroes as they race for the throne of Armello, ruled by a corrupted king. There are basically four victory options. Prestige victory: gaining prestige from completing quests
, killing banes
and heroes. Spirit Stone victory: banish the corrupted king using four spirit stones which you’ve gained through quests and stone circles. And finally, Kingslayer and Rot victory are very similar, you have to kill the king via combat and survive, when trying for Rot, your Rot needs to be higher than the king's.
+ 4 different clan containing heroes with unique abilities

+ Hex tile design
+ Day/Night cycle
+ Huge replayability
+ Four victory options
+ Interactive turn-based system
+ Cards
+ Story-driven prologue – including the tutorial. Really easy to understand and explains the game mechanics.
o Multiplayer
o Luck and random number generator
Based on the games originality, artistic design and the games narrative style, has kept me hooked to this game for so long. With heroes moving on hex based tile, and trying to get prestige, magic, coins or even rot sometimes. Quest to increase your hero’s stats, whether that be towards Fight, Body, Wits or Spirit, all depends on your game play. The amount of strategy within this game is huge which adds to the replayability of Armello.
Multiplayer, create a party or lone wolf against other competitive players, you decide. Host quit? Don’t worry, the games mechanics are good against leavers or delaying players and the AI’s still oppose quite a challenge, although, when the host drops it might result to game crash, with constant up-dates, the developers are working hard and fast to resolve this.
+ Amazing art style
+ Animations
+ Dices
- Few graphic glitches
Armello is visually stunning, and with the addition of the new seasons DLC, each season has its own glorious allures. Also combat animations with dice rolls are amazing, differing whether the dice explodes or not, also hit to the hero differs from a blocked attack. There are still some graphic glitches, but very rare and doesn’t usually affect the gameplay.
+ Stylised
+ Lisa Gerrard performance
+ Changing accordingly to the atmosphere
Soundtrack is very well created and composed. Songs are underlining the dark-fantasy atmosphere and whilst also creating a place of serenity. Lisa Gerrard participated during the composure of the sound track, her voice well known from Dead Can Dance or Gladiator suits melodies, really adds to the music’s ambience. The soundtrack is also released and made available to all, including the non-early-access players.


In game chat is disabled, this eliminates the possibility of players encountering toxic or hateful language, as this game is designed to suit players of all ages. However, the use of chat emotes allows players to communicate, regardless of their language, and to fully immerse oneself into the world of Armello, whilst retaining the character’s demeanour and tone.
Furthermore, the developers are receptive to new idea and suggestions on how to expand and improve the current chat tree.
With a little creatively, the current chat emotes can be used to forge alliances, taunt your enemies or simply express your characters emotions.

This is only one potential outcome, How will you play?!? Would you play fair? Or team up to crush those who oppose your claim to the throne. Strategy or luck, you decide, but a good player will always ensure that the odds are in their favour. This is going to be dramatic.
Hero’s traits, rings and amulets are extremely important in determining your play style during early game. An experienced player will also take tile advantages/disadvantages into account, as well as, the Day and night cycle also brings an important aspect to the game. Never attempt fate if you can help it, luck is a risk and can be terribly frustrating. Minimise the risk and ensure you equip item cards which best server your play style and repeatedly burn your cards to ensure you have the hand you want, remember, each card has a unique symbol – sword/shield/rot/wyld/sun and moon, burn these cards during combat or perils to ensure the outcome is in your favour.
Finally, be sure to watch an opponent’s move:
Money and Magic usage:  Is a good indicator of the sort of perils your up against.
States and Equipped items: Will help indicate whether you need to play aggressively or defensively.

RNG is an important part of games because it keeps things interesting. It helps people in the back pull forwards and the leaders fall into more manageable positions.
But it often times feels like you as a player are fighting RNG and not the players. It's less your strategy versus theirs and more like your fighting a coin flip.
Nonetheless I recommend this game for how fun it is with friends and family. But as a warning: Do not expect to play this game like a multiplayer with progression. It's a board game where dice and random numbers decide what happens not you; so play it as such.

The art is absolutely fantastic  and the first heist is pretty fun. Beyond that the game seems to just become a chore. So let me just list some quick pros and cons and keep it moving
- The general aesthetic of the game is pretty perfect
- 4 Player co-op is great
- The "prototype" system is pretty cool

- The menus, especially for the "clones"/"operatives" are extremely ♥♥♥♥ing confusing. Seriously, after 13 hours I still have no idea what I'm doing on the clone screen, for the most part.
- Repetition. As a fan of Shadowrun and Cyberpunk savage worlds, A majority of the kind of missions I'm used to running are "heist" types. This game does that. Great. The only problem is that it does it badly. There are no interiors to the buildings you are stealing from. You spend your time stealthing all through the vicinity of a building, and once you reach the entrance, you watch your character enter and exit. That's it. Then you leave.... What? That's not satisfying. Not at all. Try doing this over and over again with no plot to grab you, and characters you don't care about.. which brings me to my next points.
- Clones. I get the clone thing, it's ok. I get it. But this causes you to be playing characters that you don't give a single damn about. They're exactly that, nothing more than clones. Talk about boring. I'd like to be pulling off heists(or "runs", as I call them), and worry about the death of my characters. I suppose this is a matter of taste, but it's my stance.
- Sound design. The sound
. There's nothing else to say about it. It sucks. Even the ambience, it feels as if the city is completely lifeless.
- The environment. Even though I said the aesthetics of the game are great, the city still feels completely lifeless. There's no other way I can think of explaining it. It's lifeless, everything is the same.
- Micromanaging during combat is hell. Plenty of abilities to use, 4 characters to move, and no pause.
Look, honestly, I'm going to continue playing this game. if it wasn't for my absolute love of this genre, I wouldn't play this game. It's the only thing holding me in. Honestly, I should just go play Shadowrun Dragonfall or Hong Kong for the tenth time.

I played Syndicate Wars on the PC growing up.  I loved that game and the wonky things you could do with your agents and the people around you in order to complete missions.  The ambience, setting, sounds, etc, really immersed me in the game for what it was at the time.  Flash forward to Satellite Reign.  Does the game live up to Syndicate Wars?  I can't say.  It certainly looks like Syndicate wars, and the way you interact with your squad and acquire new gear is very similar to the old game.  There are some new mechanics, a fresh take on the series story wise, and the ambience and setting really captures the old syndicate wars feel.  Even the music DLC had some jamming tunes.  But that's about it.  That's about all the good I can say about the game.
It falls flat and becomes repetitious and very uninteresting.  The open-endedness of this game compared to the mission based style of Syndicate Wars is the game's downfall.  I will clarify: there isn't much interaction with the world, save hijacking people's brains, bribing, hacking, or killing.  You can't get in cars or drive, and you don't go inside of buildings and have social interactions with people.  The game is just one fluid, top down view and inventory menu, hack the same terminals, bribe the same yellow, kill the same yellow, and send agent into green door X to clear mission Y.
The research, item acquisition, cloning, and skill tree menu is about the only other thing you will see save mission briefings.  Even the level design is built like some maze where the hacker opens gates and turns off cameras, and various other dude's can turn off power or zipline, but the design fails at allowing for multiple strategies for any given security compound or mission.  Some of the locations feel cookie cutter, or uninteresting.  The reward for breaking into security compounds just feels empty because they are all so similar.  And the large military compounds are just annoying rat traps.  I am genuinely uninterested in finishing this game.  The combat, maze running, and lack of a "hook me in" with the story just makes me feel sad that a seemingly cool remake of an old gem fell short of the mark.

Bought and finished the game (launched a rocket) in 40 hours within four days. That's how addictive it is. I keep coming back to it from time to time to see new updates and try various modes, although not as passionately as the first time.
The game is basically TTD on steroids. While in TTD you "just" move passengers and goods from one place to another, in Factorio you create a system of production and transport that's as complex as the world's economy. The hours spent on figuring out why you're constantly low on that cog or advanced circuit, while your storage is full of unused copper plates, will make you appreciate the beauty of supply and demand in free markets, and how impossibly hard it is to create a well-balanced system with a centrally planned economy (i.e. you in this game).

Bug-free, addictive, dedicated developers, runs on a potato, plenty of mods.
It has a steep learning curve, but the game only formally ends when the first rocket is launched, there are plenty of goals to work for still even after that. Or just start a new base with different settings for a different experience. You can go from resources everywhere to few resources with large distances between them, from no enemies to one where the planet is covered in them, from endless worlds to a thin but infinite strip of land stretching in two directions, and that is before any mods...
If (factory) building games are for you, the gameplay time that can be got out of Factorio dwarfs most AAA titles with people having got "only" a hundred or two hours of gameplay at times being considered beginners. Community is also very friendly and helpful.

Fight The Dragon is currently in a freshly started Early Access phase, but oh boy, it already has so much potential.
The editor is easy to use and there's already a big variety of levels for everybody to play.
The Online Coop works just fine and until now I wasn't able to spot any major bugs or anything game breaking.
All in all it's fun to play alone and also with friends. I completely appreciate the splitscreen option, which is always a big plus when it comes to multiplayer!
At this point a little something about 3 Sprockets and their way of developing that game. Of course everyone is a bit critical when it comes to Early Access games, but this small team of developers has the fastest way of releasing updates I've ever seen for a game. I'm speaking of 3-4 major updates in a single week!
So yeah, great game, awesome developement team (they didn't pay me for this :D) and worth the money!

With the help of a robust, user-friendly adventure map creation tool and an already very active and tight-nit community, Fight the Dragon is an incredibly addictive social interaction unlike anything I've seen on Early Access.. or Steam in general for that matter.
Even in it's earliest form it already has a massive set of tools allowing anyone of virtually any skill level to create whatever is in their head from dark mines to open snowing forests, the variety here presented only in it's first week is enough to give every aspiring map creator the ability to conjure up something totally unique and special from one another. And this isn't taking into account the almost weekly updates the game will be receiving, already one in it's first week adding two entirely new sections of props to diversify your creations with. In short, map making is extremely addictive, often time consuming, and in the end EXTREMELY rewarding.
The gameplay itself is very fun and straightforward, almost arcade-y in a Gauntlet sort of way moreso than how modern grindy ARPGs of today play. There's already a great loot system in place that scales to your level (max 30 currently), with legendary and rare items to find that give you additional stat boosts and sometimes elemental attacks. The adventures themselves are all user-generated (outside of a small handful of high-quality maps created by the develepor to show off what you can make), which is awesome for both the person exploring levels and the people creating maps, because everyone gets a fair chance at having what they made getting played. There is one other mode, a really cool concept which the game gets it's name from where you fight a dragon in an arena with a ridiculous amount of health (millions). Killing the dragon in one, or even dozens of tries is impossible so you'll have to earn Dragon Tickets by completing Adventure maps created by the community in order to keep chipping away at it's health. There are currently no end-game rewards for the dragon that I know of (to be honest, it's so tough I don't think it's even been beaten by more than a few people yet) but it already has a leaderboard to rank you against other players based on damage done. I received the game as a gift from a friend some time ago, but held off reviewing it in order to see what direction the development team would take it.  I have to say, that after all this time, I'm pretty pleased thus far. ^^
The visuals are nice, and the boardgame-style gameplay is pretty solid.  The random chance elements in the form of the dice and various card decks encourage players to think on their feet and choose their battles carefully.
It's easy to learn, difficult to master, and fun all around.
If I had to nit-pick, my only gripe would be that there isn't enough story content.  The game only provides you with enough to understand the basic premise, but really nothing concrete beyond that; leaving you to cobble together a -very- loose narrative from the snippets of flavor text you glean from the various cards.  At the very least, they could finish giving all the player characters their back stories.

This is a game of strategy to tip the odds in your favor. Nothing is ever concrete and therefore very replayable. The memories you can make with friends are fantastic as your grand plan either suceeds for epicly fails. Whatever story your character ventures or stumbles down, odds are, you'll come back for more.
The art is fantastic and gorgeous to look at. Zooming in and out actually changes the audio you experience. The sound track and ambience are lovely and a joy to listen to.
The gameplay is unique and increasingly fun the more familiar you become with the mechanics. Hunting achievements was never something I did until I played this game.
My only request is possibly a campaign mode or maybe a new mode that has more in depth quests. I think the quests mechanic can be explored more and be used as a tool to flush out the world of Armello. Maybe even get us emotionally attached to certain characters.

I am rarely reviewing games on Steam, in fact I think this is the first ever game I have reviewed here. Heck even with the major disappointment that No Man's Sky turned out to be I stayed away from dissing the game. But this game, SGW3, is such a major bug fest that I can't keep quiet anymore. I am honestly sorry that I bought it, however since I played the game more than 2 hours, I won't even bother trying to get a refund from Steam.
First of all, we all know and love (not) the 5-8 minutes startup of the game. Every time. What I didn't realize at the time is that I have to start the game pretty much once every hour. And then add to it the 5-8 minutes of starting up and the game becomes a major waiting game.
So what happens, why do I have to start to game every hour? Well simply because while the game does work initially, as the time passes, from around 30 minutes in it starts to stutter...more and more, until there is nothing to do but wait anywhere between 10-30 seconds for the screen to load - even while I'm simply walking.
But wait, there's more.

When the one hour of game run approaches, without fail it crashes with two error messages sitting one on top of the other: "JobManager: Atomic Counter underflow" and "Sniper Ghost Warrior 3 has stopped working".
Once these error messages appear on my screen, the game doesn't close automatically. No siree. It takes its sweet time of closing - some 3-5 minutes, during which time my pc becomes completely unresponsive. Even closing it from the taskbar does nothing. Oh and speaking of the taskbar, SGW3 is the only process that is over 2 million K (close to 3 million actually) memory .
Eventually, once the pc regained its much needed balance again, I start the game hoping to get at least one mission done next time. And the cycle repeats itself. Yesterday I did this dance for 4 times no less.
Oh and if at around minute 50 I try to close the game preemptively so I avoid the whole mess, well, let's just say that things don't go any better either. I close the game, the hour glass rotates and rotates and rotates, the screen goes blank and the hour glass still rotates and rotates...you get the idea. Opening the taskbar doesn't work because everything is stuck. The only thing I'm left to do is shut down the pc. I haven't turned off my pc from the beginning of this year. Since yesterday I rebooted 3 times.
Btw before you come with 'buy a new pc', my pc is relatively new, I7 4790, 8 Gb RAM, latest Nvidia drives, the whole shebang. This setup works for every other game I have, with FPS well over 60 overall.
I posted on the game's Facebook asking for help on where to send a ticket request, and I got a boilerplate answer, something to the effect of "Sorry to hear that. We'll send that information to our dev team to fix that. Thank you for your feedback."
No, it's not a feedback I was giving, it was a cry for help.
So right now, until the game becomes playable, I'll put it aside and play instead Elite Sniper 4, which thankfully runs smoothly on my pc.

Paint the Town Red: In Early Access for roughly 3 months, priced at $9.99, entertainment value: ♥♥♥♥♥♥icly entertaining﻿.
Paint the Town Red will see you going to various locations and stabbing, slashing, punching, kicking, and brutalising everyone in sight using various weapons scattered across the map. That being said, the AI opponents populating each map will not only fight eachother, but will also attempt to stab, slash, punch, kick, and brutalize you just as much you would to them. This is also a very challenging game that will take you multiple tries to fully master the levels. If you don't feel like going through that, you can always set the optional level modifiers on. These are special "perks" if you will that give you abilities such as your fists acting as tazers. Or grant you UNLIMITED POWWWEERRRR. Spawning random weapons across the level, or the ability to turn theme off completely, leaving it to a good ol' fisticuff brawl. There are more after that, which further extend replayability.
This is the most fun I have had with an indie game in a while. I like to think of this as a mix of Minecraft (Graphics) and the blood, guts, gore, and difficulty of the Hotline Miami games. Which, suprisingly, is a sweet tasting combo. Buy it now, support these devs.

I opened up Paint the Town Red, and navigated to Pirate Cove, then set the "hard hitter" modifier on and pressed play.
I entered on a boardwalk with interesting music playing in the background. I saw a guy holding a beer mug looking at me, then walked inside the massive bar that was located right next to me, seeing a bunch of pirates drinking beer and holding daggers. I tried to ask the bartender for a shot but accidentally punched him and he went down.
Then while everyone started fighting each other, one guy came after me with a bottle and I panicked, grabbing the closest thing I could (which turned out to be a ham shank) and wacked his face a couple times before kicking him halfway across the room, knocking over a few other people in the process. Once they got up they too got angry and started heading after me, armed with glasses and daggers and even cutlasses. Scared, I sprinted up stairs, grabbing an oar that was on the wall on my way.
When I got up to the rooftop, there was a pirate with a massive sword sitting and munching on an identical ham shank, but he must have been in a bad mood because when I stepped up there he immediately got up, grabbed his sword, and charged me. Luckily my reflexes kicked in just in time and I juked him to the right, slamming my oar into his head. He flinched but kept following, and meanwhile his bodyguards started coming after me too. I dealt with them first, slamming my oar into their faces over and over until just as I had killed the last one, my oar broke.
The captain was swinging his sword down and I thought it was the end of me, but at the last moment I kicked out and my foot connected, slamming into his midsection and sending him through the guardrail and out into oblivion, where he was promptly eaten by sharks as he landed in the water. However, the other pirates from below had made their way up to the roof by now, and with no point in risking my life I jumped from the roof down and made my way to the beach.
I saw a couple of pirates fighting beside a campfire and knowing I already had plenty to deal with, I grabbed a shovel lying on some boxes nearby and kept heading down the beach. At the end there were two pirates jousting with cutlasses, and I must have interrupted them because the stopped and instead came after me.
I banged up a couple with my shovel and kicked some out to sea, but my shovel broke again and I frantically made my way up to the rocks and grabbed a harpoon lying on the edge. I was prepared to make my last stand.
Pirate after pirate flooded onto the cliff like a stream, and I just batted pirate after pirate off with my harpoon, seeing blood fly and pirates tumbling off the cliff into the sharks below. My arms were swinging full power, lodging the head of the harpoon deep within my enemy's heads, then slamming my foot into them to send them off. I must have killed 20 pirates before my harpoon, once again, broke. Seeing no other alternative, I dashed down a ladder that led to a small rock below the cliff.
The onslaught continued, pirates coming down the ladder one by one. I sparta kicked the lead and he went flying back, dislodging five others behind him and disoriented, they went into the shark-infested water to be devoured. I threw left hooks, right hooks, upper cuts, pirates dying by the dozens. But one pirate, equipped with a harpoon himself, jumped up and landed a blow that took my health down to almost nothing. My vision dizzy, I scrambled onto a small boat and onto the boardwalk, desperately trying to evade any blows.
I made by way back into the building, stumbling in with a severe limp. I saw corpses all around me, bits and pieces of them scattered around the floor. I felt faint and groped for a dagger lodged in a pirate's head, retracting it and making my way out again, to the ship that I had come here from.
The vicious cries from my tailing pirates were almost overwhelming, but I knew that I must push on, for I could not bear to lose my life this way. They were shouting obscenities, breaking bottles inside the bar as they moved through, in an effort to intimidate me. Bleeding profusely and exhausted, I stroked the wheel of my ship and vowed that I would not go down without a fight. And soon enough, the dozen or so pirates made their way up to my ship, surrounding me.
Time seemed to pass in eons in that moment, for I had a sudden burst of energy so overwhelming I felt as if I were going to faint. The mouths of the pirates slowed, their weapons in the air crawled in inches, but I had never felt as alive as I had then. It was as if the gods had infused their power into my soul, their blood into my veins. I could feel it surging through me, pulsing in time with my heartbeat, and I lifted my hands up to my face and saw blue lightning coursing through my arteries. I knew what I had to do, and with a ferocious yell, I brought my fists together.
The resounding shockwave almost blew me off my feet, and I could see the sound waves as they travelled outward from my knuckles, pulsing through the air like ripples from a drop of water. The pirate's faces contorted into looks of awe and then fear as they realized what was going to happen to them in a split second, and with a massive grin on my face the sound waves made contact.
The pirates were swept off their feet, blasted back with such force they were flipping through the air. They sailed for what seemed like years, their weapons leaving their hands, yelling and crying for help.  Flipping head over heels over and over and over again, they tumbled in a slow arc out to sea, and one by one their cries were cut short by the gulping of sharks and the bubbling of water. Splashing occurred frequently in a short time period, but it stopped no sooner then it started and the ocean was calm once again.
The moon shined bright in the sky, a full pie gleaming down on the red coat on the water. I looked back to the bar and took in the bodies, the broken bottles, the severed limbs. With a sigh of relief, the blue energy gradually left my arms and I felt tired once more, happy that I had survived. And with other deep breath, I put my hands on the wheel's embellished mahogany, and set sail for the country I had come from.
The menu popped up, and displayed a thumbnail of what they now call "Cutthroat Cove". I pumped my fists up in the air and yelled with delight, and maybe swore a few times at the pirates that had caused me such trouble. After minutes of shaking my head at what an amazing game I was playing, I finally sat down once again, and stared at the screen for a couple more minutes, frozen with awe.
Then I directed my cursor to the right once more, and pressed "play".

Played this game for a little 15 hours within few days after purchase.
So far, it's probably the best survival zombie game I've played. Its biggest downside is the lack of coop (at least 2 players would have been so awesome). If I understood well, they are making a "State of Decay 2" that will have coop, It's an amazing news. The only other concern I have about this game is there are few bugs there and there. The worse of them all: zombies clipping throught walls. It doesn't happen all the time but once in awhile and can catch you off guard.
Those are the PROS and CONS for me. Indeed, you could disagree on some of them, it's a matter of taste and point of view:
PROS:
- 1 main story, 2 DLCs that bring endless mods for super extra replayability
- Can control all survivors and have to level their abilities and gear them individually
- Permadeath of survivors
- No respawn of loot (can still establish outposts to help sustain but they wont remove need to scavenge)
- Lot of weapons
- Lot of kind of zombies
- Many spots to establish base (all your choice where your survivors will live)
- Lot of base upgrades
- Survivor relies on stamina and health to survive. Poor management of those ressources can lead to quick death (survivors are never overpowered even when well trained and well geared)
- Lot of cars with different specs (some are stronger, some are faster, some are balanced, some have better handling, etc)
- Games generate random missions to keep you busy
- When you roam around with your survivor, other survivors of your group are working aswell
- When not playing the game, stuff keep happening to your survivor (they use ressources, can get sick.. maybe not die anymore). You get an update as soon as you launch the game again.
CONS
- Few bugs there and there like zombies clipping throught walls (not happening all the time but be aware it's possible)
- No coop
Why I like this game more than many others like DayZ or WarZ or H1Z1? First: far less bugs. Then good mechanics around survivors (you have control on everyone of your community, permadeath, individual leveling/gearing, they keep living their lives while you are playing around, they keep living while game is closed)
Why I prefer it over 7 days to die? 7DtD is probably one of the most serious game out there with the most serious devs. Just I was tired of the Minecraft style of building. State of decay offers the choice where to build base, allow base upgrades but you don't have to manually build stuff. You get ressources and let other survirors doing it. If you prefer a "minecraft base building style" then go with 7 days to die. If you don't want it, State of Decay is probably the best so far.
A really good game. I got it 75% off which is absolute stealing. Even at full price, it would have worth it all the way. Definitively checking for State of decay 2.

Summary: Overall The Ballad of Gay Tony and The Lost and Damned are great standalones with slight improvements to the original GTA 4. Each one offers roughly 5-9 hours of gameplay and new elements such as parachuting, base jumping, mini-games, weapons, and vehicles. 4.5/5.
Packaged together, Episodes from Liberty City offer two standalone games that take on very different approaches to the original gameplay in GTA 4. Both offer their own single-player campaigns with roughly 5 hours of missions, mini-games, and a variety of new weapons and vehicles to spice up your experience. The stories, just like the original, are well-written and interweaves with Niko Bellic. Playing the original and then through the episodes will give a second perspective on who did what, where the diamonds came from, and so on. They aren't heavily dependent on knowing the original plot, but they can be better appreciated if you've played through it.
The Lost and Damned takes the perspective of Johnny Klebitz, the vice-president of The Lost Motorcycle Club (TLMC). As you would expect, you primarily travel by motorcycle and much of the storyline is around the MC and their conflict with the police, rival gangs, and eventually the mafia.  There is a healthy heaping of new music revolving around the 1% culture, weapons such as the sawn-off shotgun and grenade launcher, and mini-games in the clubhouse such as arm-wrestling and air hockey. One of the big improvements, at least in my eyes, is the use of mid-mission respawns. If you die or fail a mission, restarting it via phone will no longer pull you to the very beginning of the mission. You will probably respawn before the segment where you failed, started. This cuts down on the amount of needless driving when you fail a mission and makes it less of a hassle restarting.
The second episode is the Ballad of Gay Tony, which doesn't take you from the perspective of the flamboyantly gay Tony Prince (whom you may have noticed in Niko's story), but his bodyguard and partner Luis Lopez. If TLAD focused on motorcycles, it's safe to say that TBGT focused on helicopters, base jumping, parachuting, and night clubs. Again, TBGT's plot is interwoven into the original plot and fleshes out much of the why's and how's of that story. As with TLAD, there's almost a good half-dozen new mini-games, such as golf, dancing, drinking, parachuting, and races. If you had a hard time with the helicopter controls, then bad news, about 1/4 of the missions require piloting a helicopter at some point. Generally the storyline is well-written, the characters are great with Yusuf, the playboy millionaire Arab, Mori, the bodybuilding dwarf with a God complex, and Bulgarin, the Russian mobster collecting American rock memoribilia. The characters drive the storyline well and leaves the game with a satisfying conclusion.
Overall the game improves on a few issues from the original, but there are still a few things that hamper your gaming experience. Controls are still finicky, with driving still painful (you'll come to hate motorcycles on the final TBGT mission), flight controls difficult, and shooting still frustrating at times. It'll put a smile on your face when you see an NPC struggle to get in and out of a vehicle, but make you cringe when your characters' pathing causes him to dart back-and-forth around a vehicle. Mission restart has been improved, maybe some way of fast-travel would make driving less of a burden but I'm sure they want the playtime to be buffed higher by needless traveling. In summary, it's a strong buy and I highly recommend the game, I think that if you especially like the original then you'll find enjoyment with the episodes. 4.5/5.

​Lets start with my biases; I've played both Syndicate and Syndicate Wars, and have also played similarly themed games like System Shock 1 and 2 as well as similarly styled games like jagged alliance, XCOM and Xenonauts.
It is a cyberpunk themed, top down, open world, squad based, real time, tactical shooter with RPG elements. It is not turn based and for the most it is not pauseable (however there are character skills that can emulate pausing or slowing down the action). This is probably the biggest change for players who are used to the slower pacing of turn based games like XCom and is probably the biggest gripe from people who try to pick it up, so much so that it makes you wonder how the game would have turned out if they had taken the turn based approach (or even real time exploration, turn based combat like fallout 1 and 2). In this way it plays a bit more like a Hero style RTS.
You're pretty weak at the start, and have very few abilities and upgrades, so the result of my first firefight was a total party wipeout which, while a bit frustrating, goes to show that while it is a real-time game you need to approach each encounter and situation with some tactics and planning. This is partly because the enemies you face are, in many ways, equally tough and similarly equpped leading to less player/AI asymmetry than most games resulting in situations where if you get outnumbered you'll die.
In essence, you play each mission on a knife edge, delicately managing stealth and minor skirmishes as you progress through a hostile location, trying not to "awaken the tiger" and create an escalating alert with an increasing and overwhelming enemy response.
The game does have a reasonably steep learning curve, and it keeps throwing new gear, augmentations and skills at you resulting in a steady progression of new tactics to learn and integrate. By the end game you'll have a tough, adaptable team with a wide variety of offensive, defensive, diversionary and stealth skills providing an extensive toolkit to deal with the different location, environmental and enemy type situations.
The RPG elements align roughly in this way; Stat progression is mainly a combination of clones (base stats) and augmentations (enhancements), Durability is a combination of shields, armour and health, Gear and Skills overlap a bit by providing a mix of enhancements to Stats and Durability as well as the RPG style Abilities or "Spells". Weapons play a less pronounced role in itemisation compared to most games of its type and mainly provide a scissors/paper/rock element against shields/armor/organic opponents. i.e. plasma weapons defeat body armor, laser weapons defeat shields, etc.
Certainly, one of the most fun parts is how often your well laid strategic plan on how to tackle an enemy base can very quickly fall apart and descend into frenetic chaos. You're now making choices like which party member to revive, or even abandon on the field as you try to force a retreat *through* an overpowering enemy that has suddenly surrounded you. While it can be very frustrating to experience a total party wipe it goes to highlight the "knife edge" nature of the game I mentioned earlier.
On the other side, there's nothing like the rush of salvaging a &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥hits the fan" situation; suddenly getting detected, having the base on full alert, getting surrounded and overwhelmed, but somehow managing to scrape up your fallen team, manouver them out of the killzone in a retreating skirmish, then find a place to patch yourself up then re-enter the killzone back in control of the situation.
The open world and variable nature of the game along with the randomisation of enemy types and placements can lead to situations where you get wiped in your first attempt only to walk through it in your second which means the game focuses more on your ability to adapt to rapidly changing situations rather than to have a well thought out plan going in.
Sometimes I wish there was more to do as you wandered around the city, more opportunities to interact with the locals, more side quests, more story and more background. The main plot is pretty straightforward and a lot more could have been done to develop the lore and flesh out the factions and make it more engaging. I know I'm fighting Eternals, but who are they, what do they believe and how does that fit into the Satellite Reign universe.
Finally, the story has elements of the grand, but plays more as a straight "level up and kill the boss" type game. While some people don't care for the back story, they could have done a lot more to flesh it out.
Yes, absolutely. It has also recently delivered on its kickstarter promise and released co-op gameplay.
If you're really into the tactical turn based games, like XCom, etc. you might find the change of pace to a real time tactical shooter a bit too frenetic. But if you're willing to step outside your comfort zone and embrace the real time mayhem, you'll find an excellent game.

TY the Tasmanian Tiger was one of my favorite PS2-era games of all time. It always surprised me how lukewarm the critics were towards it (most dismissed it as a soulless, but serviceable Mario or Banjo-Kazooie clone). Nothing could be farther from the truth than that.
Pros:
+Unique, almost comforting atmosphere. This game is beautiful. No other way to say it. The levels/environments you explore are varied and detailed. ranging from the Outback desert, quiet rainforests, the Great Barrier Reef (probably my favorite), snowy mountains, etc.
+Phenomenal soundtrack helps set the mood for each environment and is jam-packed with catchy, memorable, relaxing, intense, and even uplifting tunes (it's that good).
+Boss fights are intense, creative, and challenging.
+Gameplay can be addicting. Think of it as something like Donkey Kong 64, only much more streamlined and less tedious. It's an adventure platformer with collectathon elements. The large, beautiful environments really inspire you to go exploring.
+Great controls.
+Balanced difficulty. It's just challenging enough to avoid feeling like a cakewalk.
Cons:
-Some of the more hardcore players might find it too easy.
Port quality: Really nice so far. The visuals benefit from a nice upgrade, with improved resolution, a maxed out draw distance (climb to the tallest point in the level Ship Rex and you'll see what I mean), a silky smooth framerate (locked 60 FPS), improved shadow effects, better use of color, and more to come. Very responsive controls too. The game feels vastly more playable and comfortable on PC than the original PS2  outing. The only cons so far are a few very minor frame drops (and stuttering) in some levels as well as brief graphical glitches here and there. Also, it would be really nice to see some more improvement on the textures as they look almost identical to the PS2 version (albeit with a higher resolution). Also, the cutscenes are locked at a somewhat choppy 30 FPS for some reason. Can't wait to see how the finised product will look and feel, seeing as the devs are constantly updating the game to fix any bugs or glitches (as well as improve the graphics further).
Overall: Worth a purchase. Probably the best 3D adventure platformer out on Steam at the moment and what looks to be a terrific port of an awesome game from days gone by.

I had a blast reliving my childhood when I played this game! Could not put it down untill I got 100% in the game. I highly recommend Ty the Tasmanian Tiger to anyone looking to get away from the FPS grind and need to play something different. My only problem I had with the game was figuring out how to swim fast, originally continued to double tap the space bar but I see that it has been fixed in a patch now. Never got the chance to play TY2 in my childhood but look forward to when it comes out!

For those of you who played Ty in the past, consider buying this port and supporting these developers to add more content, fix more bugs, and port the Ty sequel games to PC in the future. They've so far showed devotion and hard work towards getting this game out of early access with the best quality they can manage. And there are some new extras that are a treat to old Ty fans.
For those of you who haven't, this game is basically one of the old classic platformer collectathons of the past, but with cool, unique features like the boomerang weapon, which is very satisfying to throw and glide with. Not to mention some collectibles are actually really hard to find at times, so there adds and extra layer of challenge for treasure hunting.
Speaking of difficult, I will admit this game wasn't too difficult so far, maybe that's just me having played this 12 years ago, or I've played many platformers. I'm more leaning towards the latter, so if you're crazy about platformer collectathons, expect Banjo Kazzoie levels of challenge from this game besides the ocassional speed-run challenge or wild turkey chase. But I will say the heart of this game is not for its difficulty but its diverse and somewhat open-ended levels. Just exploring the levels and finding all the things to collect while you glide, swim, look around corners and ditches and hige rooftops, it's quite fun.
This PC port of the classic game has been optimized to work at the highest of framerates on the lowest graphic settings, trumping the PS2 in terms of performance. And the highest graphic settings add so much more detail and scenic beauty to the original, but is only recommended for high-end PC's.
Overall, a must buy for fans of Ty, and a good pick for those looking for a good platformer collectathon while you wait for Yooka Laylee. ;)

I'm usually more verbose with these reviews and my explanations of the game mechanics, but I feel like explaining too much of the game mechanics is a bit of a spoiler for this game. Basically, you collect resources, manage production and conveyor belts, and defend your base from hostiles. Automating resource collection and production is highly satisfying, and if any of that sounds even remotely interesting to you, I can recommend this game with confidence.
This is a game I easily see myself still playing 10 years down the line. Complex enough that you get that same feeling when you complete a line as you do when you complete a SpaceChem/Infinifactory puzzle, yet casual enough that I was able to get people that were turned off by SpaceChem/Infinifactory's difficulty hooked on this game. The campaign does a great job of easing you into the mechanics and teaching you some efficient ways to make factories too. Abso-freaking-lutely worth the $20, wish I bought it sooner.

This game seems to be a lot better than I would've ever expected. It's great for Star Wars fans especially those whom love the Clone Wars. It's extremely fun to actually be commanding a squad rather than being the "newest recruit" in the squad. You're all brought up the same way and you all became part of a team together which really puts the equality between your team. The great thing about this is rather than viewing them by their rank, despite that they're all pretty much the same in this game anyway, you can view them by what they're specialized in.
Another great thing about this game is that your character can actually talk! YES! You read this correctly! Unlike almost EVERY other FPS, your character can talk! And he talks as much as the rest of the squad which can lead to some really interesting conversations between the squad.
However, as with every other game, there are some flaws. This game can be INCREDIBLY difficult which really puts people like me off of playing it. Because who wants to play the same mission 100 times just to move to the next, even harder, section of the mission. If you're someone who hates having to search up walkthroughs, good luck trying to complete this without going to YouTube. Another flaw that links in with this, normally games use hints for you to find out how to get around a certain enemy in this game. As much as I've focused on the surroundings, enemies AND dialogue, I haven't noticed any hints since Geonosis.
To sum up, for someone who hates a lot of FPS games I really enjoy this and I will continue to play it... When I can be bothered to look up the walkthrough for the mission on the Acclamator-class Assualt ship.

A highly enjoyable game with lots of potential. This review is based on Early Access: Alpha 2.1. The concept of this game is simple, explore an array of user generated dungeons to acquire equipment and improve your character, currently only the Fighter & Fire Lord are available to play.
The games combat system is simple and well defined, though I am not entirely comfortable with the controllers interface, I found myself continuosly trying to open( X ) an enemy rather than attack them. Perhaps allow for controller remapping, or provide a map that uses the Left/Right Triggers for combat?
Enemy characters look exceptional and are initially enjoyable to slay, however after a few levels I found myself killing the same monsters with little variance in their combat tactics, most monsetrs operate on a run towards player and attack strategy.
The game provides a swathe of equipment, with some rather enjoyable names, running through a dungeon can easily see your backpack being full of primarily junk items which you don't seem to be able to sell anywhere. In fact you can accumulate money but I'm not sure where you spend it?
Dungeons can feel slightly bland with monsters only being used as the main challenge, hopefully as users become more familiar with the map-editor and the editor provides more tools to create unique set-pieces that provide memorable engagements this will be satiated.
Overall I found the game exceptionally enjoyable to play, but as it is Early Access lacking some of the components that could make it a truly great game. I look forward to seeing more from the developer, 3 Sprockets.

Boring game with bunch of mind-less repeating missions. Takes away a bunch of player freedom for the sake of being "realistic" e.g. no manual saving and not even ♥♥♥♥ing pausing the game when looking at the map. No fast travel despite the huge map so you have to drive for ~30 minutes for some missions. This may be just me but I think the zombies respawn way too fast as well. You also have to use 100 influence (the in-game currency) to hire a follower yet the leave as soon as you start a mission without refunding the influence so you have to go and grind the influence again. Story in the game in non-existent as far a in can tell in my playthrough except for the typical "world has gone to♥♥♥♥♥♥so we gotta band together to survive".

The main problem with the game are the bugs. It starts with setting the resolution. Interestingly the game doesn't accept 1440p, it's either 1080p or 4K. Another thing is the quality setting which is restricted to max by default although you can get a modded config from the nexus that unlocks ultra settings. There you can also get 2K texture packs and other mods to enhance your gameplay experience.
The most annoying bug are the flickering shadows in 4K that can drive you crazy. There's a no-shadow mod to circumvent the problem but I think that's not a valid option to fix this bug. Better try Realistic Shadows Mod - SweetFX - FOR VANILLA - FOR BREAKDOWN - FOR LIFELINE by SilentResident on the nexus.
The zombies clipping through walls are a minor issue in comparison.
All these bugs that still exist after years hold the game back from being a great game instead of being only above average.
Despite the bugs which can mostly be squashed using mods it's an interesting game and you can experience memorable moments while playing. The game world is detailed and large with no loading screens thanks to the CryEngine.
I can't recommend the game at full price. Although it's well worth your money if it goes on sale for under €10 and if you have the patience to do some work on polishing the game yourself with mods. In the condition SOD is sold I rate it 6.5, with mods it is 8.5/10.

Backed this game on Kickstarter, it's really come a long way. Armello is an absolute gem of a game. A digital board game featuring lovable animal characters trying to dethrone a corrupted king and claim the throne for their clan. Mechanics are well thought out, and the game is regularly updated with new and improved systems to add additional depth while not making the game overly complex or confusing. There are multiple ways to win, which helps keep a single person from dominating the match, though the game is quite RNG-based, relying on dice rolling for battles, card drawing, procedurally generated board, semi-randomized quests, and a few other mechanics. Sometimes even with excellent strategy, the luck of the draw can't be overcome.
Still, an excellent game I never get bored of.
Game length: 1-2 hours
Pros:
+ Beautiful and unique style and graphics featuring anthropomorphic animals
+ Great soundtrack
+ Procedurally generated board means every game will be different
+ Multiple ways to claim victory, to stop a single player from dominating and blocking others from winning
+ Interesting and unique systems for combat, bounties, and 'traps'
+ Each character has a unique hero power that makes them different from other heroes
+ Each hero can be further customized to your playstyle with a selection of rings (exclusive to clans) and amulets (available to all heros)
+ 'Microtransactions' handled very well and very positively for everyone. Dice skins can be found in chests and traded or sold on the Steam market, which the Devs get a cut of when an item sells on the market.
+ Updated fairly regularly with new and enhanced systems
+ Devs are very attentive to bugs and glitches and do their best to solve them as soon as they can
+ Promotes public play with a chest and key system, in which both chests AND keys drop
+ Custom rule settings for private games
+ Can play a single-player match while waiting for a game (though queues are rarely very long), tab on taskbar will flash when you find a game while queued is you don't want to play singleplayer
Cons:
- RNG-based, sometimes too much
- Some hero's powers are almost useless, while others are very powerful
- Private play doesn't give you keys or chests, making those who prefer to play only with friends unrewarded and left out (though the keys and chests only contain cosmetic dice skins, so it's not a mechanical disadvantage)
- Currently a set of 4 exclusive Kickstarter heroes, though anyone playing in a private game with someone who owns them can use them, they can only be used in private games, and the Devs have stated they will be released as DLC for anyone to purchase eventually
- Only way to communicate is through a set of 'commands', such as Hello, Good-bye, etc. No voice or text chat.
- DLC is a little pricey, especially in comparison to the full game (the set of 4 DLC heroes is $10, 2 board skins are $5).

I really wanted to like this game but there were a few design choices that made it frustrating to play.
+ Nice cyberpunk art style.
+ Variety of weapons and powers to aquire.
+ Earn money over time by hacking ATMs, so no grinding for currency.
- Focus on stealth, but no option to save scum.
- Team is always Soldier/Support/Hacker/Infilitrator, no changing this, limits team compositions.
- AI have long, complicated patrol routes, makes sneaking hard.
- High enemy health (shields and armor) limit options for sneak attacks.
- Alarms can create infinite enemies.
- Hacked doors reset after a time, often blocking escape if stealth fails.
- Complicated controls, e.g. assign group selection to F-keys needs to be redone each time the game loads or the team dies.
- Little penalty for dying, so the game seems to intend for it to happen a lot, but that doesn't make it less annoying.
- Missions are mostly flavor text, little-to-no voice acting.
- Real-time combat + lots of abilities + four team mates + no tactical pause = micromanagement hell.
- Cannot turn camera, makes it hard to view some locations.
I played for a few hours, then reached a mission where I spent 15 minutes sneaking in, only to make a mistake and my team gets killed.  OK, no matter, I'll try going in from the other side.  30 minutes later, after 2 emergancy retreats and dozens of masterful assassinations, a freshly spawned guard spots my team running behind some dumpsters, fires of a few shots, and seconds later two dozen armored guards have us pinned down and we got slaughtered again.  That was when I rage quit.
Honestly, save scumming would have redeemed this game for me, but I'm rather a stealth perfectionist.

If not, at least make it so I don't have to wait 2 mins for the game to load, then immediatly run into a bug (like the tutorial suddenly starting over, 3 hours into the game) and have to load it AGAIN. The world-building and the story are all classic cyberpunk, with corporations taking over the world, technology advancing too rapidly for its own sake, and so on and so forth. The storyline is mostly about listening to audio messages and reading background information, it features few characters and the ideas being discussed aren't particularly noteworthy. The ends justify the means in this world, and anything from open street warfare to civilian brainwashing and hijacking is permitted. The player controls four agents from a corporation trying to rival the all-powerful Dracogenics, their goal to bring it down via espionage, sabotage and street fights.
Each soldier can take a hit like a champ and is able to sabotage vital power generators and mechanical targets. Hackers can hijack security systems, enemy drones and even civilians or soldiers thanks to their brain implants. Support is responsible for healing the squad and, more vitally, scanning the world for targets of opportunity or weaknesses in enemy fortifications. Infiltrators are basically ninjas who are able to get into areas others can't via air ducts and zip lines. He or she can also wield a sword or sniper rifle with deadly precision. Every agent is distinctive, and all the roles can be further enhanced as they gain more experience.
The early game can get a bit formulaic with the limited options, but the more you play, the more possibilities you have for various situations.
The city is divided into several sectors with different themes ranging from industrial to high-end residential. Each has their own main and side missions to complete to help with bringing down Dracogenics and their allies.
AI pathfinding is somewhat of an issue for both you and the opposition. You troops can get stuck between a ledge and a potted plant while running for cover. Enemy troops can get stuck on a door, furiously trying to run through it even if it's closed.
It might not be a bug-free, smooth experience, but it probably offers the best real-time cyberpunk that's available right now.
- Cyberpunk setting
- Agent upgrades
- Pathfinding
- Weak story

Why didn't I start this game ages ago?
Satellite Reign is a spiritual successor to Syndicate, a classic strategy game from the 90s. SR creates an impressive open city that is fun to explore walk around in. You can zoom the camera all the way down and get a good look at the advertisements on the buildings and the dystopia of cyber street life.
The open city is split into 4 districts each with relays (fast travel, gear stations) and ATMs which can be hacked to increase your steady income. In each district are guarded areas to infiltrate in order to get bonuses to the district. And the regular story missions will take you into these areas to proceed through the game.
These guarded areas make the game. It truly is free form in nature with  multiple ways to sneak in or shoot your way in. I once got my infiltrator on a high roof and sniped every guard in the place without being seen. Another complex had my infiltrator stuck behind enemy lines with no easy way out, and my other 3 guys went through HELL to try to get her out only to have my entire team wipe during ex-filtration. On the way back into the complex to get the blueprints I found an air duct that lead to a much easier way in. Since there is little penalty for death, you are free to try something, fail, and then try something new. There is a sense of satisfaction of finding the right plan of attack, getting in and getting out with no problems. Or even getting in quietly, getting the objective, only to get into a massive firefight on the way out, then getting everyone out alive. It's like beating a hard boss in Dark Souls but I felt this way after every mission. Each mission was its own story in a way.
SR is a real time strategy game, with an option to turn on "team stims" which turns on bullet time so you can get your bearings and issue commands. I was finding new stuff to do in the game right up the every end when I discovered that hijacking was very powerful.
I recommend this game. But you need to go in with an open mind. It's not for everyone. I actually bought this a long time ago, but only got into it recently. Once I started playing, I was hooked tho. So your experience might be different.

On the surface this looks like a really stupid and poorly done game.  First impressions are really quite awful.  You have to give this one some time in order to fully appreciate it.
Starting out, it is just you, stranded on a planet with raw resources.  Gathering them is slow and tedious.  As you gather more resources, and develop more automation, gradually the beauty of this incredibly elegant game becomes more and more obvious.
There is no other game I have ever seen like Factorio.  In general I am someone who plays a lot of RTS games.  This is similar to that genre, and that is the closest match, but it is so much more robust than any other RTS I have played.
If you like a game that makes you think and is constantly giving you issues to resolve, this is a perfect game.  It is very reasonably priced.  Don't be put off by how boring it looks at the beginning.  I have played this solo, LAN with my son, and online.  All modes have their pros and cons.
If you are interested enough in Factorio to actually be reading this review, just buy it.  You won't be disappointed.  For the price you can't find a better value.

A quaint little action/adventure-ish game with puzzle elements thrown in, created by the Ubisoft studio that made the recent Rayman games and Child of Light. Set in the First World War, it revolves around four main characters and their ordeals during the conflict, and left me with a case of the feels by the end. If you have any interest in war history or just want a nice short story-rich experience, give it a try.

It's a pretty good puzzle game.  The story is catching with a very few "too real" scenes thrown in.  It isn't Life is Strange or Undertale, and you probably won't walk away with a new outlook on WW1.  I liked playing it.  If you end up playing it and liking it you should try reading Fall of Giants by Ken Follet. It's the best Fictionalization of WW1.

1 – GENERAL
Alien Swarm: Reactive Drop is a free to play, top-down shooter. In this game we have a team and we have to control them and kill the alien hordes to reach the end of each level.
Sound effects and voice acting are good enough. The graphics are also more than enough to have a very good free to play game. The game has a story, but I admit that I have not pay much attention to it, so I assume it's there to try to give some substance to gameplay, or I would have noticed it better.
2 – GAMEPLAY
You can choose from 4 different classes, each one of those kinda unique. Each one with 2 weapons. You aim and shoot with the mouse, and sometimes you lost track of where you are aiming, but that is a minor issue. I've not found any problems with gameplay.
You can play solo or online with a group of other players. Playing solo is quite good. It's easy to command the other team members, and they are good enough not to stand in your way.
Playing with other people is very fun and way better to work as a group. There's ingame voice so you can talk with other people and that makes things even easier.
There's some different missions, each one of those can give you around 1 hour of gameplay, and you can repeat them a lot of times without getting tired, so I have to say that the length of the game and it's replay value are quite good.
You can add mods to the game, and that makes it even more interesting.
3– CONCLUSION
There's nothing in this game that clearly shines. There's also nothing that really disappoints. What intrigues me the most is that there's nothing to buy here, and for a completely free game I have to say that it is a quite good one, and you will have a lot of fun before you get tired of it, so just try it.
