It was a typical night in town. Day 11 so far. Morale is starting to lower and one of our members  is beginning to let fear get the better of him. This needed to be fixed before a crisis would occur. This would be Jacob’s second new mission and so far so good with him. As Jacob, I took our fellow survivor out to kill some Zeds to loosen him up and it was going well so far. Until a random Feral came out and ripped Jacob in half before I had a chance to munch on my energy bar. It was terrible, just terrible…and also pretty cool. At its best, this is what State of Decay is all about. It’s random, enticing, devastating, and exciting all in one package. But there a few major problems that keep this from being a satisfying experience.
Gameplay
State of Decay is a Survival Action-Horror game with RPG elements. Set up in a small town, you are thrust into a zombie infested world which acts as a hostile playground for players to explore. Your ultimate goal is to create a surviving community until military evac arrives. Gameplay involves fighting via third person hand-to-hand combat and shooting. As you progress, the community you help build will begin to expand and gain the ability to create infirmaries, libraries, etc. And the survivors that you play will begin to develop their own skills such as shooting, fighting, and wits while out doing missions or searching for supplies. The catch is that there is only a single save file with permadeath enabled. If a survivor is killed, morale drops and you’re switched to the next survivor. Progressing through the game requires story missions, side quests such as interacting and helping strangers and fellow friends alike while trying to survive another day.
There is so much to do and explore in this game. Exploring your environment constantly brings a sense of danger around every corner and comes with its own risk/reward system. Finding supplies is uplifting and all, but making sure you have a plan for getting back is necessary as Murphy’s Law can and will happen.
Managing your community means making sure that everyone is well fed, mentally and physically healthy, etc. As you progress through the game your community can continue to expand to different areas as a means of safe zones to prevent zombie hordes and other problems from arising. Honestly, I found this aspect of the game to rather shallow for specific reasons. For one, you can’t manage what other NPC’s should be doing; nor could you send your companions out to various locations for errand runs. Instead, you drive all the way over to the location and then decide to bring a runner, should you not have enough space in your inventory to take a load back home. This resulted in lots of precious time being wasted and monotonous at times. Not only that, at random times I would be making a long drive to a mission only for one of my runners to be trapped by a bunch of zombies, resulting in me having to drive all the hell back just to save them. This happened so many times that I had lost count.
Combat is surprisingly satisfying. Approaching combat requires to weigh the odds for each method. Do you go all in with melee to avoid attracting other zombies or do you take them out from afar with your gun while potentially compromising your location? Monitoring your health is not the only important bar to pay attention as each character has their own specific amount of stamina that you need to pay attention to. Running out of stamina spells out your doom and requires a strategic mind to maintain while fighting. With the various amount of fighting abilities and specialties for each character, experiencing combat with each character was consistently fresh and exciting.
Driving in the game is on the neutral side of things. Cars get you around but some have terrible and unrealistic handling.
What brings the gameplay down are the extraordinary amount of bugs that you will encounter in the game. I can’t count how many times a zombie would spawn right next to me, ruining my attempted stealth run. Sometimes, zombies would simply spawn out in mid-air while you are driving and there was a time where I was forced to reset my game because I encountered a bug that would not allow me to talk or interact with options. For a game to have been around so long, it is quite disappointing to see such problems take you out of the experience. Don’t get me wrong, this is a very fun game to play, but the problems are as obvious as white on red.
Narrative
There is barely any story to really mention in this game. What I mentioned in the intro paragraph is what the story is basically about. There are story missions which are all unremarkable and side missions which help flesh out some of the characters in this world. It would have been nice to see more consequences for the death of a fellow survivor rather than a simple notification or some obviously sad music for five or so seconds. Consequently, this aspect severely affected my enjoyment of the game as barely any conversations are meaningful and are combined with shallow responses from your player character during side missions.
Speaking of side missions, they’re mostly fetch quests with some go rescue this shoved inside. These missions have a timer on them unlike the main quests and not fulfilling them can result in a death sentence or loss of potential relationship building. Having to decide on which side quest to pursue is great and all but it is consistently bogged down by repetition and lack of surprise.
Graphics
What stands out are the various environments you will visit throughout the game. Despite having ugly and blurry textures reminiscent of an early Xbox 360 game. The environment is pleasant to look at, but what isn’t pleasant are the god-awful character meshes and textures. Combine that with static animations and robotic conversations, the graphics department is a bit of a mixed bag. Though the combat animations are quite satisfying to view.
Sound
This game wins in the sound department. Whether it’s hearing the satisfying crunch of a zombie’s skull being smashed or when firing your weapon, this game works well with what it has. Voice acting is at times decent and other’s just terrible. But the music itself was perfect all around
Ending Execution
This is what almost killed the game for me. After a very tense fight with multiple hordes of zombies, you get a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥cutscene with a few bits of dialogue and then the game ends, achievement unlocked. This was lazy, pointless, and pretty much failed to impact in any way possible. It was so anti-climatic that I kind of felt I wasted my time with the game. This method of ending a video game is shoddy, lazy, and shameful.
Originality
Today, there is an insurmountable amount of survival based zombie games now. But few have it done it as well as State of Decay. None of the gameplay really stands out, but the experience of success, loss, and just epic failure will stick around in your gaming memories forever. But its terrible graphics, bugs, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending keeps me from recommending it to anyone.

What if...
What if Dolfy, through his occult studies and expeditions, found a way to revive the dead? Well, he would obviously create his Nazi Zombie Army!!!
And that's all I can say about the plot as I never really paid too much attention to it. There's no need to. I could also tell you about the gameplay, but actually there's not much to say, the gameplay essentially is the same as in Sniper elite v2 but this time with zombies. Levels are simply tunnels where you have to stop here and there and face the zombie waves.
Very quick, very superficial. Because there's no need to go in depth, nor to say too much. Such a simple premise and a recycled gameplay mix just give an amazingly and incredibly fun gameplay, as long as you play cooperatively with friends, of course. This is the kind of game you just play and have fun because you play with friends and it doesn't need any particular story, nor complicated mechanics, just go and shoot or snipe on the hordes, that's all, really. Why the fun? Friends of mine just love wave based coop games... Or zombie games. I can live with it but I've been simply struck by the 80's synth music and that foggy atmosphere that really reminds me of Carpenter's movies. That's my weak point: 80s. Believe me or not that made the difference to me with other common games: the opportunity to play with friends against nazi zombies in foggy villages with an 80's synth music.
I could spend a couple of words about the awesomeness of the slowmotion effect during successful sniping shots and the x-ray cam to see which bone has been broken by our bullet, but that's not the news, something already seen and already done, in Sniper Elite v2 or in Mortal Kombat as well.
The most important thing I can say is that this is the first chapter, there's a second chapter and there's a trilogy chapter, which holds the first, second and third exclusive episode in an improved engine (not much, just a little bit).
So while I recommend this game, I actually recommend you to buy directly the trilogy because this situation doesn't make much sense at all...

: The point & click genre is well represented as you pick up a whole assortment of objects and trinkets on your adventure, using them and combining them in creative and often funny ways to progress in the story. You come across a couple of strange or wacky characters on your adventure, and there's a few out-of-place reference to other games and movies in a hit-and-miss attempt to mimic the humor found in golden age Sierra and LucasArts games. The voice acting is ok, at least for the most part, and backgrounds look like the caricatural hand drawn style you'd expect. The story is child-friendly, and you must keep in mind that it's likely the target audience of the game as there is little to no jokes, not even subtle ones, targeted at a more mature audience.
: The characters' 3D sprites clash strongly with the 2D cartoony background, and I'm not convinced it was the best choice. The story is short, and the puzzles aren't enough to make it the lengthy experience a

The theme of the game is around the Caribbean Sea. You’re a young pirate woman who wants to prove to everyone that you can be the next best pirate captain. You have a lot of obstacles and convincing of others in order to make this dream happen. You’ll encounter rivals and haters who will want to end your dreams. There are some moments where the female protagonist has to help others out on their own personal agenda in order to progress further on her own adventure (this gives a bit more background story on those individual characters that help you along your journey).
As long as you have an open mind, don’t hate pirates, know that this isn’t a RPG; like treasures and an adventure – I would recommend this game to anyone who likes point and click games. I did enjoy this game and would give a 7/10.

This is the closest thing to a proper single player zombie game that's ever been invented.  I recommend this game hesitently knowing how scummy the devs are that made the game (they released a very buggy game and then re-released it with bug fixes and charged full price rebranding it as a new game).  That being said, the game is actually so good I'm willing to put aside my morals and say if you are looking for a proper single player zombie game, this is the best that you will find.
It still has some bugs, and there are many things I wish they would change, but overall the game kicks♥♥♥♥♥
Things I wish were changed:
-I wish they made the game mod-able so we could see awesome community driven content
-I wish there was a proper element of human vs. human combat and politics.  As it stands the game is really just humans vs. zombies
-I wish there were more maps for the sandbox mode, or better yet randomly generated maps
-Along the same lines I wish you could make your base in any structure on the map
-I wish that the "management" aspects of the games allowed you to pause the game.  I'd like to review my characters while back at home base and make plans for my base without half a day worth of gametime passing
Things I love about this game:
-The combat is very well done.  When you are overwhelmed by zombies there is always a chance to beat the odds and survive, which feels absolutely epic when you pull it off, but at the same time the brutal death scenes and permadeath make the death sting that much more. This entire portion of the game is beautifully executed.  A+
-The base building and managment aspects of the game are far better than I expected.  It is so fun having a base and a community of survivors you have to care for.  This is one of the coolest aspects of the game and something I haven't seen properly done in any other zombie games (they usually just focus on you as a sole survivor).  There's room for improvement here but as it stands it is the best you'll get from this genre of games.
-If you are a fan of The Walking Dead, this is the closest game you will find to emulating that experience.
-The map is very well designed and the main storyline was actually pretty decent.
Overall it's the best Zombie game out there and I don't foresee any others surpassing it any time soon unless some amazing Fallout 4 zombie mod gets made.  If you can look past your morals and just buy this version of the game you'll have a good time.

First off i would recommend to buy it on a sale but if you think this game got everything you want for a zombie survival game, who am i to tell you what to do.
You start at the lake where you spent some time with your friend but then some cannibals (because they dont seem to know what a zombie is) are trying to get a piece of you.
Here i tell you a bit of the content:
-Base building: After a while you find your destination to your first home the church at those homes you can resupply, rest, switch your character, etc. If you are sick of the little room you have you can get a new home with more space BUT you can only have one base. Also you can choose what your base contains for example more beds or a garden to produce food.
-Zombies: Normal zombies are fast or not its a surprise, but the troublemakers are the freaks. Freaks are mutated zombies with special abilities like pin you on the ground or just smash you. Every Zombie is sensitive to sound so its an advantage or disadvantage, because while they can hear you they can also hear fireworks and other distractions.
-Survivors: You can get more and more survivors to join you, but you have to win their trust. Every survivor is different and if they die they stay dead. If your character is tired or wounded you can choose one of the other survivors in your home.
-Map: The map is large and contains small towns, big cities, farms and a military base.
-Cars: In this game you can choose between a medium cast of cars some have more place in the trunk, others are faster, etc. But cars make a lot of noise wich attracts the undead and you are driving a car not a tank so it dont take much to destroy them.
-Loot: You can find everything you need to survive weapons, snacks, firecracker, ammo, painkillers, everything. But you are not the only one taking the supplies you need to keep your home stocked with food, ammo, medicine, building materials and oil.
-Gamemodes: In "State of Decay:YOSE" you get 3 modes but they arent that different. The modes are:
State of Decay (basic), Breakdown (Harder than the basic mode with big hordes attacking your home in waves) and Lifeline (Basicly the basic gamemode except you are the military)
-Conclusion: I enjoyed State of Decay because its a solid survival game with great gameplay elements and this game makes sure you wont run out of zombies. I hope i could help you out with this little review, have a lovely day!

I have played 2 hours and 30 minutes of this game so far, and I AM LOVING IT. The game has you play as a Clone Commando, designated "Delta 38". Your squad (Also named "Delta") are also highly trained clone commandos. The graphics aren't terrible (in fact, I kinda like them) despite the fact that this game is pretty old. It took me a while to get used to the controls, as mouse 3 is Aim, not right click (which is grenade).  Gameplay is VERY solid, and FUN. Its starts out easy, but quickly gets DIFFICULT, even on the normal mode.  And in the beginning, when you dont know how to counter the enemies, it can take anywhere from 30 seconds to 2 minutes to destroy new enemies, such as Super Battle Droids. But that is quickly remedied when you have the tools and experience.  The AI is actually REALLY good, as in, unlike games like Call of Duty, the friendly AI can actually shoot and kill things. This is really helful, especially when there is many or tough enemies. Also, since we're on friendly AI characters, I LOVE THEM. All your fellow Commandos, despite being clones, are very human so far. They have different personalities, and in the short time I knew them, I started caring about my "brothers".  Although there are some Friendly Fire incidents (both me and my squad's fault) I felt like this made them even more "human" (probably due to the ammount of friendly fire that happens in other games like Arma or Insurgency). You can also give your team orders, which I find to be promptly followed and well executed, which has been a huge assist. So in conclusion, I will list what Ive found;
-Solid shooter gameplay
-Nice, easy, and fun squad based mechanics
-Many different enemies in the campaign
-Human like characters (For me anyway)
-ACTUALLY HELPFUL TEAM AI (very important)
-Very Very Fun.
-graphics are still alright (depending on your tolerance to old graphics)
The few bad things I have found are:
-Enemies sometimes bug and dont move or shoot
-Allies sometimes get stuck on a position, making them take a while to execute the order.
-old graphics

The best way to describe Inexistence is Order of Ecclesia on Super Nintendo. It starts out kind of linear and then you hit the main castle which is more explorative requiring backtracking in order to continue forward. I like the sprite work and the enemy designs, at worst, are too cute to destroy. It's an action rpg so leveling up is the norm with the ability to configure where your stat points go for customization which allows for different play styles. The music is pretty good and there are different weapons, armors, and accessories to collect to help move your journey along. Don't expect a cavalcade of content as this is a bite-sized adventure, clocking in at about 2-3 hours which can be multiplied by three as this game offers three modes of play. Having purchased the game for two dollars and my personal affinity for simplicity and Castlevania; you would think that this is a match made in heaven except...
I've played this game twice and if you were to ask me what the story is about the best I can come up with is that you're a boy trying to save his sister from a curse that was put on her by a bad man. I don't even remember what the ending was and I just finished it about twelve hours ago for the second time. There is only about 1 full page of dialouge in total and sadly none of it was memorable enough for me to even care. At least an attempt ws made, though. The enemies, while cute, are bland and stale with some of them being completely unable to turn around or pose a decent threat. The bosses aren't much better, either. Each boss possesses 1-3 attacks and can be dispatched extremely easy depending on your level. Basically, if you want a real challenge, don't level up. Even the final boss was pathetic despite having three forms which is mostly due to the insane amount of bugs that this game has. First of all, if you're an achievement ♥♥♥♥♥ then prepare for frustration as bugs can prevent items from spawning, chests from being opened, and your game completely being corrupted beyond repair. During my playthrough, the reason why I played it twice is because there is a glitch that happens when you save while an enemy flies in and kills you. You get warped to a wall causing you to be unable to escape which means your game is ruined. During the third form of the final boss he can't damage you sometimes so steam rolling him is a cake walk requiring no real strategy. All of these imperfections lead into an ending that is as mediocre as the game itself.
If you are not a completionist or you can avoid said glitches then get this game for a buck if you want but considering that this game has been out for a year and there is a myriad of unacceptable problems; I would seriously suggest that you avoid this title. $6 is an insane price for this game and don't even get me started on the "bundle" offer. It's a shame to see a potentially decent game get passed over because enough time and care wasn't put into the finished product.

Quick Summary: Basically the same game as Magicka 1, but with improved graphics, new magicks, and a new story. I found the game to be more difficult to complete than the first as well, particularly since the enemies have more varied weaknesses/resistances this time around. I liked the first game, so I enjoyed the second one as well.
You play a nameless wizard on a quest to save a “chosen” child with a grand destiny, under the supervision of Vlad the not-vampire from the first game. Along the way you’ll encounter a huge variety of pop culture references and humor, just like the first game, as well as some powerful new enemies. In the first game, you could get through almost the whole campaign relying on arcane mines and steam+lightning beams, but this time around, you’ll need to switch up your spell casting or you’ll get stomped by enemies resisting/absorbing your spells. Of course, multi-player co-op is again available and you can (should) play through the campaign with your friends.
For people who’ve played Magicka 1, here are the main differences:
Magicks can now be quick-cast by pressing preset cast buttons (1-4). You no longer need to memorize long elemental combos to case awesome magicks. However, magicks now have a cooldown time. The cooldown is lower if you type in the elemental combo rather than use the quick cast, but you still can’t flood the screen with the good stuff.
A lot of the basic spell combos have been changed. (No more EARS mines, now it’s a steam wall). The Healing mines from the first game (EW) detonate much slower and are less powerful so don’t rely on them to save you. You also can’t use arcane mines to blast people off cliffs as easily.
You now “unlock” gear such as robes (with bonuses and negatives), weapons, and staves by completing campaign levels and finding secrets. I suppose unlocking items is better than needing to buy DLC.
No more ‘checkpoints’ for resurrection. Your familiar sacrifices itself to resurrect you when you die, and you can immediately cast Revive to bring it back to life. This means you can die as much as you want, as long as you cast revive fast enough.
For people who haven’t played Magicka 1:
You control your wizard with the mouse in isometric view (like Diablo or Torchlight) and cast spells by combining elements with the QWER and ASDF keys. Each key is an element (for example Q is water) and by creating elemental combinations you cast spells (SFA = death+fire+lightning = fiery lightning beam). The order of elements doesn’t matter as long as certain “opposites” aren’t in there. For example lightning will cancel water. You can also cast “magicks” which are powerful spells with unique effects using preset elemental combinations (also use the space bar to cast instead of mouse buttons). For example life+lightning casts Revive, which can resurrect your dead ally (or familiar). Some of the magicks from the first game have been nerfed (lightning bolt), but some of the new magicks are great for single player (lightning birds!).
Pros:
+Has the good parts of the first game. Fun story, nice graphics, co-op gameplay, and a lot of humor
+More people are playing this online than Magicka 1, so you can pretty easily find someone to play with, at least on normal difficulty.
+So far, you don’t miss out on anything by not owning a ton of DLC. The first game had like a dozen different DLC to purchase.
+A lot of the things you unlock during the campaign are “artifacts” which are basically just small modifications to game difficulty. For example enemy damage +10% or speed -10%. This allows you to create some unusual difficulty customizations.
Cons:
-The game’s achievements have a lot of “grinds.” For example, kill 10,000 enemies or die 1000 times. It would take 100 years to get some of those unless you ‘boost.’ There are also a number of very difficult “challenges” or “trials” with achievements. If you generally only play a game until you finish the campaign, resign yourself to having about 30% achievement completion for Magicka 2.
-Despite not looking that much prettier than the first game, Magicka 2 has noticeably higher system requirements. I also encountered this weird bug where the game will reset the resolution every time I start it. It only takes a minute to set the resolution again, but it’s annoying.
Overall, Magicka 2 is a great game that is better with friends. If you take it slow, you can probably beat the highest difficulty by yourself, but what’s the fun in that.

This game is dull.  My friend and I got it to play together because it sounded like it could be fun; but we were very wrong.
The game, at first, seems alright.  The graphics are fine.  Nothing really stands out as being bad.  You go through a tutorial learning how the mechanics work.  Friendly fire is always a fun way to troll your friend (and boy do I like to troll my friend.) And the game is fun for the first couple of chapters.  But then it starts getting repetitive.  It's just you dealing with changing waves of monsters.  Over and over again.  You don't level up.  Your magic doesn't improve.  You don't find better loot.  (I mean, you do find new weapons/robes/staffs but they're not necesarilly stronger; they just may fit your play style better.) So My friend and I played one night together.  It was fun.  We played the next night together and it was still fun at first but by the end of that play session, we were bored of the game.  Only a few hours into the game.
The gameplay just isn't unique enough to be fun as is.  It's essentially "spray magic elements" at waves of enemies. You can get more advanced with your attacks.  You can put shields on yourself.  You can apply magic to you sword.  There are different combinations of magic you can cast and it can but fun to mess around with.  But it's all temporary.  It gets very tiring of having to recast the same magic over and over again.  There is a hot bar for quick access to some spells, but there should really be a customizable hotbar for your personal combos you like to make.
And to be fair, the lousy gameplay would be fine if it at least had a good story.  But it's not a good story.  It tries to be funny but fails.  It's filled with small references to everything but in a way that's just not funny.  More just random than anything.  By the end of our 2nd play session, we were just skipping the dialogue because it was absolutely pointless and a waste of time.
So.  Boring gameplay. Dull story.  Terrible jokes.  (and not even the good kind that are still kinda funny like Dad jokes.  just really bad jokes.)  Would not reccomend.

Great point and click adventure.
I completed the adventure as it should be completed, with no hints or peeks at walkthroughs. It took me about 18 hours, so those people who claim to have finished this in 6 hours can only have used walkthroughs.
There are 10 chapters and each chapter progresses the story very nicely.
What I loved about this title was the dialogue, which was funny and made perfect sense. The voices of the many characters were all really well done and very much added to the atmosphere. Some of the characters are particularly brilliant, such as the debonnaire but daft Briscoe, the fabulous Buck who reminded me of so many people I've met in SE Asia (the developers really nailed that character), Sonia is the most hilarious and cagey dock side 'worker' ever, and of course the lead character, Morgaine, is a superb act. There are many more great and wacky characters that will be encountered that really do a great job.
The story is very interesting and really gets going in chapter 2. I have seen reviews criticising chapter 1, but it's a cute, short introductory chapter and great for story background. and takes about 45 minutes to playthrough. The ultimate quest, introduced by the eccentric English gentleman, Briscoe, is always the aim, though the journey there will take many twists and turns with lots of side quests.
I don't want to give away any of the plot, but I'll just say that the way the story dealt with a sad death was very touching indeed and one of the peaks of the title.
The graphics are bright and colourful and their cartoony style do the story lots of justice. Well done to the graphics team.
The puzzles are mostly fetch quests, dialogue threads and inventory matching. While these are mostly fun and do require thought and LOTS of experimentation, it would have been nice to have thrown in some other types of puzzles too. The few mini game type puzzles are on the weak side,
I liked the control system of clicking the dialogue to move it on as that way I didn't miss any important information and it allowed me to read it while listening, at my own speed. A good system. The inventory, as mentioned above, does require a lot of trial and error, but is perfectly fine.
So, overall, I really enjoyed this game, though I was not sure I would before I started playing it. I would strongly recommend it for  15 plus very entertaining hours (if played with no hints).

Star Wars Republic Commando is an fps game released in the star wars universe in 2005. In 2015 it still remains one of the best Star War games ever to be created and im trully sad to admit, i didnt appreciate it in its time of release. Back at the time i felt the game was really hard even on normal and i couldnt get accustomised with the various game mechanics. Now that im a bit older (but certaintly not wiser ^^), i came to appreciate this awesome title in all its grandeur.
In this game you play the leader of a republic commando team, whose purpose is espionage,sabotage and advanced reconnaisssance. Obviously stealth is out of the question for like 95% of the game but the rest are yours for the making. Your team includes 3 more members each specializing in its own field. You get your sniper, your demo man and your enginneer as well. Throughout the game you are called to make tactical decisions and place your team8s around the field, in order to maximize your chances of survival and win your confrontations. Its sounds easy to do and at first it is, but as the game evolves your desicions must evolve as well.  All and all that was one aspect i enjoyed the most in this game.
As with any good fps, you get to use a lot of different weapons and grenades and you can further enchance your own weapons to meet any kind of enemy. From the simple laser pistol to a full rocket launcher, this game has it all and more.
In terms of gameplay difficulty, the game is not as hard as you might think, but its harder that most of todays standard measures. You dont get to do rambo stuff, cause you will be facing the ground and w8 for your m8s to revive you and that is really nervebreaking. All the levels have a linear design as well, so you wont miss your next objective. Maybe for most that is considered a down, but i think it works pretty well for this game.
The graphics arent on par with todays standards, but you can modify the texture pack anyway you like and you can increase the games resolution as well. On the plus side even if you dont it still looks ♥♥♥♥ing awesome. And as with any star wars game that respects itself, the audio is one of the best things in this game. Everything from the tiniest footstep to the biggest blast has been exceptional and thats something i cant say for most games these days.The dialogues are grimm and funny at the same time and the voices seem to match everyone and everything in this game.
All and all i recommend this game to everyone. If you are a fan of fps you will love it, if you are a fan of star wars you will love it even more and even if you dont like fps try it. You will love it too!!!

Grand Theft Auto: Episodes from Liberty City is a standalone compilation of the episodes for the 2008 video game Grand Theft Auto IV. Created by Rockstar North in the United Kingdom, it contains both The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony on one disc.[1] It was released alongside the DLC release of The Ballad of Gay Tony on 29 October, 2009 for the Xbox 360 and released on 13 April, 2010 for Microsoft Windows and PlayStation 3.
Unlike the downloadable versions of the episodes, the compilation does not require a copy of Grand Theft Auto IV to play, nor is an Xbox Live or PlayStation Network account necessary (except for multiplayer). The content is also played straight from the disc, and does not need to be installed on a hard drive to play, like various other disc-based expansions for other Xbox 360 games that have been released in the past. Available exclusively on the Episodes from Liberty City disc are three new in-game radio stations – Vice City FM, RamJam FM and Self-Actualization FM.

Presenting GTA IV's Liberty City in two entirely different lights, these two games offer several hours each of extra missions and new characters, all set in the same world as the main game.

The focus on motorbikes (specifically choppers) is a nice move away from a focus on cars.
The Ballad of Gay Tony demonstrates the lighter, brighter side of Liberty City, far more in line with Vice City's glitzy parody of Miami.

You do not need the original Alien Swarm downloaded nor do you need to play it. Reactive Drop is a straight upgrade and a standalone. It has everything from the original game and more.
Alien Swarm: Reactive Drop is (mostly) a cooperative game playable with up to 8 players. There's a fair amount of challenge depending on your difficulty and playstyles. I was overjoyed when a game I'm fairly familiar with comes up with new territory. But they are not without flaws, both old and new.
Since the game is practically the same, it shares the same cons. I didn't mention it before so this will be the whole package.
The level up system sucks. You unlock one item every level, something you might not ever use, like the flashlight. Thus, not every level is going to be worth your while. Of course, leveling up increases the experience required for the next one. Easy, up until the 4th promo and beyond. The grind is atrocious from here and the items you unlock are probably not the one you want to be using 90% of the time. There's 3 equipment slots and 31 levels. I mathed. Praise me. A-anyway, if you're coming back to the game like me, and you want those promos, you know how it feels. If you're new and you want to be doing this kind of thing because you're a masochist, congratulations, and welcome to the club.
As you can tell from topic above (I hope), equipments are not balanced. Some items are just better than the other, giving you no reason to use the latter. Now, if that's originally what the game intended to do with the level up system, that wouldn't be a problem. However, this is not a powercreep game. Equipments you unlock early can rival those you unlock at much higher levels and can leave you quite dry for a very long time if you don't get something good.
I'll admit. I judge people by their skill level when I see what they pick as their loadout. My point above.
There is a large skill gap between players. Most experienced players who have played on the highest difficulty will instinctively rush through the levels as fast as they can while avoiding whatever they can, and the new ones will turtle to fight everything they see. If you've never played the game before you don't understand that this is a bad idea. Pewpews are limited. Aliens are not.
Pub games are littered with these two types of players. The slower group lack the experience to defend themselves, often getting swarmed to death and forced to spectate the rushers. It's not very fun for them. I think I can tell.
I don't want to dissuade you, I'm just not a very good person when it comes to praising something... or anything really. My "friends" know. They get insults instead of praises. (I love them though. Honest.)
Regardless, Alien Swarm is pretty gud.
Play with friends and play casual. Or else suffer pointless grind.

Love Alien Swarm. This fan-made revival of Alien Swarm adds new weapons, a handful of new campaigns, and options for up to 8 player coop. All the strong basics of Alien Swarm are still there and it's still as addicting and fun as the original. Also it's cool how it's tried to more directly integrate community-made mods to the game, extending its playability as you add weapon skins, character models, and even more campaigns.
That being said, the game suffers from very poor matchmaking. Numerous times it's impossible to connect to certain public games and I have never successfully managed to set up a Deathmatch game, either in a private game with friends on in public. Always some issue with connection kicks people out specifically for DM.
There are also bugs that need to be ironed out. On occasion, selecting a different character becomes a nightmare as the character doesn't change even after selection. This has happened a couple times and I've managed to bulldoze through it just by selecting enough times, but it appears often enough to be an annoyance.
Many of the new campaigns were once fan-made mods and so usually lack the polish of the base campaign. No voiceovers, as limited as that was in the original. That said, they usually make up for it with the ingenuity of the settings.
I give it a 6/10, but with the potential to be an 8 or 9 if bugs are cleaned up and the fiasco with matchmaking is improved.

Inexisistence is a fun, short, simple 'metroidvania' style game.  If you know what you're doing, you can easily 100% the game in less than an hour.  The gameplay is relatively shallow.  Unlike most Metroidvania games, you start off Inexistence having access to most of the gameplay mechanics and character progression is extremely simple and rudimentary.
Now, all of that may sound negative, but I actually really enjoyed my experience with the game.  Sure, there are more compelling games within the genre, but I think there is definitely value to a game that provides a charming, enjoyable experience in a small package.  I also especially enjoy when I encounter a game I've never heard of, and it turns out to be such a solid package.  I thought the art looked great, the controls were fluid, and it is clear that the developer was attempting to say something with the story, however sparse the exposition was.  There is also a Time Trial mode with a leaderboard, so I think this game has some speedrun potential.  I beat this game 3 times to get all of the achievements, and it never felt like a chore to replay the game.  I should also note that the game is a pretty easy game, even on hard difficulty.
More than anything, though, this game made me really excited for the upcoming Inexistence: Rebirth.  I think Inexistence is a very competant first game, and I think there is a lot of untapped potential, so I really look forward to seeing where the developer takes it.  I hope that both the mechanics and the story are delved into, and fleshed out further, but I look forward to the result.
Inexistence is definitely worth an afternoon or evening of your time and on sale is a no-brainer.

The following is a 1080 Review of Inexistence.
First our tale of the tape:
Inexistence
Jonathan BRASSAUD
Metroidvania RPG
$5.99
Inexistence is a Metroidvania that involves a pair of siblings.  The sister of the pair is placed under a curse and it is up to the brother to free her from the curse.   The island that make up the world is broken up into four six sections, each with their own degree of difficulty that is scaled up from the previous area.  The first two areas are relatively easy to get you through the mechanics of the game (aka the tutorial section), the latter of the two contains the only shop in the game.  While the classic Symphony of the Night does contain only one shop, the difference here is that this game doesn't refill non curative items at all, and you go into most areas blind.  In fact the only area in the game that you do have some sense of awareness of where you are is the castle area, and that is because there is a map provided for you as the only map that you can buy in the shop.
That said, not all is bad.  Enemies do have some scale of difficulty, however, most are defeated if you actually use your level up points in any decent distribution system.  In one of the most graphcially flawed systems of distributing points ever, There might be some confusion as to whether or not there is a cap that is supposed to be placed on stats as I was able to break through the HP stat cap in a few levels.
That said, I find the story to be most disappointing, and it left me wanting more.  If there is going to be a sequel to this game, I hope that a few plot points that were left open in this game are addressed in the sequel.
Pros:
+ A fun little Metroidvania that provides decent challenge and difficulty
+ RPG Elements does provide added skill to the game.
+The collectability factor does provide an additional story.
Cons:
- The story is a bit bland and left me wanting more.
- You are entering most of the game completely blind.
- The store doesn't refill any non-curative items.
The Final Score is a 5/10 - Average
I do not recommend at this time.

Things you need to know (but aren't shown anywhere):
1) In the steam game folder, use 'settings.exe' to change resolution and toggle fullscreen/windowed mode.
2) In order to use items, right-click to open the menu, then left-click and drag the item towards the bottom of the screen (to exit the menu while holding the item), hover over the thing you want to use it on and then let go of the mouse button.
3) You can combine items in the menu by dragging one onto another.
4) The menu has a map that lets you move to other areas later in the game.

This reviews probably won't count for alot of people because I'm personally not much of a Star Wars fan.
The game had interesting conscepts and I never played it when it was first released way back when so I think I missed out when this game was top of the line.
The sound in this game is pretty badass, the music is great and the dialog between your squadmates is cleaver in giving them well rounded personalities.
The graphics vary throughout the game in my opinion, the first are you start in looked like crap to me with terrible textures and bland empty areas, but when you're inside of ships or helping out the wookies there's more design put into the levels it seems so it actually gets better thoughout the game.
The AI annoyed the hell out of me, you need to tell them to do every little thing, if you leave them alone during a fight for even a few seconds they'll find the worst cover possible like under a turret or in the line of fire of a super battle droid and get utterly destroyed. This ends up being a chain reaction sometimes since you other squadmates will then run to the downed person and try to revive them getting shredded by the same damage that started the problem in the first place. They continuously walked in front of my fire, a few times they walked in front of me just as I was tossing a grenade so it bounced back and took most of my health.
The guns are probably the worst part for me, you get a pistol, assault rifle, sniper, anti armor rocket, and a special weapon. But the reticles for them are just horrible. The assault rifle is the worst just being a huge circle that you fire pretty much on the right side of. The ammo caps for the weapons are really low too, making it so you spend some of the game swimming in ammo you can't even pick up, and then other parts in the game completely tapped out for long stretches of time (Except for the worst gun for the situation like the energy shotgun special weapon in a long range encounter).
There isn't that many enemy types, just bugs, droids, and lizards. The main issue is that droids like the droidika and the super battle droid are largely bullet sponges, which in itself wouldn't be bad in order to toss a little bit of a need to focus fire in the mix, but towards the end of the game they send droves of super battle droids at you, and given how much ammo you waste on them I actually found it easier to just grenade them as a distraction then circle strafe around them and melee them to death (A ridiculous tactic that really breaks the seriousness of everything but it saves on ammo and actually resulted in me getting shot less).
Pros:
Great soundtrack
Squad dialog is pretty entertaining
Wookies (They're huge and pretty viscious but they tend to just run into fire and die)
Cons:
Graphics are dated
AI
Guns
Waves of bullet sponge enemies as you go further
Buggy (Tell squadmates to take up snipe positions and watch them target things out of their line of site, or not switch to the sniper and proceed to try and hit long range targets with terrible accruacy weapons. Had a few get stuck in some place and stop following me.)
I doubt they changed much since this game came out so if you liked it then you'd like it now. I just wasn't the correct audience for this particular game and it got pretty dull towards the end.

A not so long time ago in a country not far far away came a game so good we would ask for a sequel for ten years after release and still has not got one yet. This is star wars Republic Commandos. In the introduction you are shown the early years of a clone through quick clips of training introducing your squad. Your excellently written and acted squad is comprised of Fixer, the hacker and technical expert, Sev who is the hunter and sniper of the group who jokes around with Scorch, the demolitions expert who is always telling jokes at the worst of times. You and your squad fight on iconic planets from the movies such as Geonosis and Kashyyyk doing missons such as killing geonosian leaders, blowing up droid factories and saving wookie generals. The game is a first person shooter (obviously) with some strategy elements involved via squad commands such as ordering your troops to move to tactical positions, provide covering fire, attack targeted enemies and seize objectives. Certain actions will play to a commando's strengths like Sev is the best with a sniper and Scorch arms explosives faster and Fixer hacks quicker. This game looks good even though it came out about a decade ago and has really nice level design. The campaign is short lasting about 5-7 hours but it makes you eager for more and the story set up a sequel which we unfortunately never got but i hope that one day we will. All in all i give this game an 8/10, i would have rated if the campaign was slightly longer.

While Sniper Ghost Warrior 3 may not be perfect  it  HAS been a lot of fun. Granted I have played less than an hour but I like what I have played and seen so far in this open world.
CI Games has redeemed themselves by doing a good job with SGW3 and hopefully they will continue to deliver and improve.
The rig I am running SGW3 is at the highest settings for my 4k setup which is a Core i7 6700K, eVGA 1080 (381.65) and I receive 60 fps, which is by far a huge improvement since the beta!

7/10  My score is based on first impressions after several hours of gameplay, with the potential to improve with regular patches and updates. Hopefully the game will only get better with future patches, fixes, gameplay enhancements, planned MP and DLC content.
So far I'm actually really enjoying the game. If you liked Far Cry 3 and enjoy stealthy sniper gaming but are okay with that experience not being completely polished, I think you'll enjoy Sniper Ghost Warrior 3. It's a HUGE improvement over their previous Sniper titles and is a nice reboot for the series.
For a lower budget game I think SGW3 is a great deal and offers many hours of fun, sniper combat gameplay. Although the story is very generic, the main missions and side missions are actually quite fun and intense. You can easily die after only a few shots and the AI can be relentless once they coordinate and find your location. As a result, planning ahead and succesfully taking out numerous enemies at an outpost/base/stronghold is very rewarding.
I only paid $30 USD which also included the Season Pass. It's supposed to take 30+ hours to complete on a single playthough which is more than I can say for many single player only games that cost much more and can be finished in under 10 hours.
On the technical side, it's running great on my system. I'm currently playing on max settings at 1080p with 60 fps locked. Load times are very fast as well.
I will update my review as I progress further into the game. Thanks for reading my review gamers!
* System Specs *
i7-6700K @ 4.6 GHz
Nvidia GTX 1070 (Asus Turbo, OC'd)
16 GB RAM (G.Skill DDR4 3200 MHz)
Installed on SSD

**Short Review**
It's like an older CoD Modern Warfare game tried to branch out into Sniper Elite mechanics, and brought nothing innovative along the way. The enemies feel like card board targets and headshots don't have that rewarding feeling we all crave. I've only played a bit of the game and the dialogue feels like it was written by a teenager who watches straight to television war dramas.
**FIXED AS OF 4/27/17** The in-game options at the time of this review have no option to disable motion blur on it's own. There are no FoV settings in the base menus either.
On the plus side, difficulty levels feels very well balanced, keybind customization is solid, and game runs with no dips on max settings at 60 fps. I've crashed 3 times in 6 hours. (I have a gtx 1080 and a 6700k).
I could never recommend this game to anyone unless you haven't played a shooting game in 10 years and want something "new". It's alright if you haven't touched the Sniper Elite franchise. But the game simply has nothing interesting to me.
I should also add, this game doesn't look as good as it looked in the screenshots. I was pretty underwhelmed, although graphics don't make a game!
*Reminder: This unorganized review is just an opinion and should not be a primary factor in you not purchasing a game. Just a personal nudge!*

This game claims to be a Metroidvania style game, and while it's clear it tries to be that, it fails.
To start this game looks clunky, the sprite work is average and the monster designs have no consistency. In the later levels you'll just see tinted replicas of past monsters. Items are the same image with recolors to make them look a little different. Backgrounds can somtimes look good but the cave level's background flickers! For no reason!
Gameplay is a crap shoot, platforming is a total slog since you have to stop ever couple of seconds to slap a monster with your metal stick. Monsters rarely offer any challange and all fall to spamming the attack button. You have magic but it starts with low damage and ( in my run ) was always totally useless. It would only offer a ranged way to kill things.
You have a doge jump, for some reason, I never used it since wacking with the sword a few more times was often a better method to deal with any incoming hit. That or just jumping.
Exploration in this game is also useless, they inform you that certain walls can be walked thorugh, and some can be phased through, but they never have any clue as to WHICH walls can be accessed in this way. So if you want to find everything you have to slam your head against the walls. The game offers you seven puzzle pieces to find and collect, but it doesn't show you how many pieces are in each level, leaving you to rerun levels over and over again just to hope you can eventually find it. If you care enough to.
The game is perfectly beatable without them, this is because this game is an RPG.
What this means is any boss is beatable by simply leveling up your HP to its max, or doing what I did and maxing your attack to quickly kill bosses. Bosses attacks are utterly wimpy, the first two simply summoning falling rocks that you can easily dodge, or not even dodge as they don't seem to lock onto you! The final boss was a bit more challenging, but was easily powered through via the use of potions, which you can buy from a shop.
To top it all off this game is SHORT its so gosh darn short. I played 4.5 hours, and I cooked and ate dinner in that time! This game isn't worth 5.99, it's debatable if it's worth a dollar.
If you want to see what can make a platformer bad, buy this on a sale, other than that stay away!

STEAM, please give us a middle button that reflects neither good or bad against a game.
I've been a gamer for a very long time and I actually enjoyed playing through this one; however, it has some glaring faults that need to be mentioned.
On the plus side it's easy, would be ideal for someone's first metroidvania to introduce them to the genre. The graphics are ok, clean and crisp and remind me of old SNES fare. The story is minimal and the ending is rather dark if you read into it. It is a very short game and as others have pointed out, achievement hunting is about the only reason to play it a second time or even on hard mode. The level design is ok, much like old SNES games there are a lot of little hidden areas.
In the negative side of things the level design allows for a lot of cheap hits and not much creativity in playing through. Only 4 armors, swords, and amulets, all of which seem to bump your stats up. The abilites you have to find, metroid style and there is some backtracking you can do with them to get to other areas. Your appearance and attacks do not change with the new gear and the new abilities which is disappointing to me and the abilities really don't come into play with the combat. You gain experience and it's easy to level up fast just by going back and forth between rooms/areas and killing the bad guys. Once you max your health and either your magic or sword attacks you just do more damage.
I'm not saying this is a bad game at all. It does not deserve to be called garbage or insulted but I can't recommend it. Maybe as a mobile game it would work a little better. If it is the developer's first effort then I would say it is better than I could do and it was fun. (I know, if I had fun then why not recommend it?) It just needed MORE. I wanted MORE. Some tweaks, some added levels and it would have been a solid title to me. (Keep in mind that this is my point of view.)
If you are ok with the things I mentioned above then take a chance on it and you might have a bit of fun. I do not regret purchasing it by any means, I just really wish it lived up to the potential it had.

On the outside, ecotone looks like a typical indie platformer. Each level is physically disconnected from the next and there is no story exposition, no cutscenes. But once a few levels have been played, the game shows how it truly stands out from the crowd: the mechanics can be completely different from one level to the next. All these modifications are inspired from other platformers. Time stopping from Braid, gravity switch from VVVVVV, size changing from Mario/Rayman, and so on. An element that comes back a few times (albeit with different twists) is the mind-bending ability to control two characters at the same time.
As a consequence, it is really hard to get bored while playing this game. It is short enough not to overstay its welcome (5h to 100%) and well worth its asking price. Some mechanics are so fun that I would have loved to see them stay a bit more. However, some rare levels here and there can be really difficult and frustrating. I would not recommend this game to people that are not platformer enthusiasts. Of course it is not as difficult as the later levels of Super Meat Boy or I Wanna Be The Guy, but still, do not think that the cute art style does not hide some tough as nails sections. My real problem with these tough levels is that I believe that they are made harder by the way the character handles. It is fine everywhere but in these specific levels, like the one about jumping in between shadows (the character slides slightly too much after moving) and the final level about jumping in between tight spaces (crouching while jumping is rather counter-intuitive, and hard to perform according to your control scheme). The good thing is that since the mechanics and levels keep changing, anything that is not appreciated does not bother again.
My main criticism is actually quite vain: there are no achievements :(
As this game borrows mechanics from others, it risks being hollow and have no personality on its own. Thankfully it's not the case here, thanks to the overall art style. Unique, great, it feels both eerie and mysterious. I would enjoy to know more about this bizarre world infested by black worms and fireflies. The music supporting the game is great, even if a tad too dramatic for atmospheric levels.
ecotone is a love letter to the whole platformer genre, borrowing mechanics here and there to surprise the player and make each level become a completely new experience. It is cute and pulls its own weight. I recommend it to anyone that enjoys indie platformers.

I've really enjoyed my time playing through Ecotone, the creepy-cute artstyle bleeds into every part of every level. The sound design is pretty on point with the varying level background music reinforcing the sombre atmosphere.
What I like most about Ecotone is how it changes up mechanics on each level throughout the game, some of these changes are fairly subtle, but often enough the alterations totally change how you play the game.
This could easily be super confusing but each level is prefaced with a little phrase which gives a clue to what to do for the level and for the most part its intuitive enough anyway. These clues stitch together to give the game what amounts to its story.Whilst the story more or less fits the sombre atmosphere of the game, I'm not sure its executed fantastically, plot arcs that seem to be building feel like they aren't resolved properly, though I suppose that sadly mirrors real life in many cases. Another problem is that sometimes the phrases have to be awkwardly worded in order to both fit the current level, and fit itself into the wider narrative which can be a bit jarring.
Without going into spoiler territory, I found the ending the game goes with very surprising and confusing, I mean I could just be a moron but it made me feel like I had missed something in terms of the story that seemed to be being told throughout the game. And the bonus epilogue chapters didn't really help in that regard, even though they did deliver more of the off-beat platforming I'd been enjoying.
So far as difficulty goes, Ecotone doesn't require the level of platforming skill and dexterity of, say Super Meat Boy, but its still not exactly a cakewalk either, mercifully death in the game allows you to get back into the action quickly, which may not be unusual in challenging platformers these days but it certainly saves on frustration. The difficulty curve throughout the game is a little strange, there are a couple of early levels where its pretty easy to sabotage yourself early on, requiring a level restart, but beyond those early spikes, the difficulty curve is pretty smooth.
So, if you like platforming and enjoy the artstyle you've been seeing for most of this video, and the idea of a game changing up its mechanics from level to level interests you, then ecotone could well be right up your alley.

To all of the grouchy Squidwards who are poised to strike and dislike, you can gripe and complain about the way I wrote something very informed and to-the-point, but make it be known that I honestly couldn't care less. That goes ditto for doing it on other peoples' reviews. It's just pointless. But anyways...
State of Decay, in my opinion, comes with three games. The base game and its two expansion packs, but the thing is that all three each share their own style of play, which I'll break down. If any of these are to your liking, I insist you buy this game. Once I've finished covering the three different games, I'll explain the similarities. Sound good?
State of Decay; base game, is my least-played mode despite how story-oriented it is. I can't put my finger on what the hell I don't find attractive in it, but bottom line, I don't put much time in it. Still, it gives you the tutorial of everything SoD-related, and has a strong emphasis on the caretaking of NPC's, and trying to escape certain doom. If you want a zombie game with a plot, and one that is more focused on keeping yourself and your community in this apocalypse alive, this should be a steal for you.
Breakdown; my favorite, goes for a neverending, open-world experience that was highly requested of the developers. Breakdown has no end - unlike State of Decay and Lifeline, which both end once you finish all of the quests, Breakdown has no plot-oriented quests or ultimate ending. It's entirely focused on gathering loot, building a community, slaying zombies, and just seeing how far you can get before you ultimately lose everybody you love. Breakdown is the best part of State of Decay: YOSE, because of how limitless it is. If you want a zombie game that stresses open-world, limitless zombie survival with a sole focus on PVE, Breakdown was brought down from heaven and into the Steam Store, just for you.
Lifeline is a considerable challenge. It turns the difficulty up to the highest mark, and makes the gathering of resources much harder, so as a result, my Army FOB started out healthy and strong, and is now looking like my local Pizza Hut (the one with the bullet hole in the window). To add further insult to injury, unlike Breakdown and State of Decay, which have zombie "assaults" as mere skirmishes with hordes that pass by your settlement, this one has zombies that mass up and slam you in overwhelming waves. It's actually kind of frightening. If you want a serious challenge, Lifeline provides.
All three games share the same mechanics and controls - one big thing about State of Decay is permadeath. Each character has one life. Nobody (except for one character in Breakdown) has plot armor; everybody is highly susceptible to being torn in half (the zombies seem to favor that execution over all others), and as a result should be treated with extreme caution. What puts great stress on this point is that each character has different skills and talents, which can be leveled and improved, so that makes them even more precious.
In stiff contrast to Dead Island, for example, there is an equal focus on melee and firearms, which I do like since I adore guns. Just as well, since, like Red Dead Redemption: Undead Nightmare, Zeds only go down with a bullet or a baseball bat to the cranium (headshots), with the exception of any .50 caliber weapons, which can kill zombies with one shot anywhere, fire, and explosives/explosions. Guns are especially useful when you consider that these zombies are actually quite sharp - they move fast and attack fast. As a developer said in an interview, if you're dealing with say, two zombies in close proximity; no sweat if you know what you're doing. More than two, and things get problematic. Melee encounters with hordes are desperate pleas for death.
So ultimately what this game offers is three different variants of the same game, but they all share the same focus on building a community and rescuing other survivors. I highly recommend this game.

It's a fun game, if a little short. It's challenging if you try to play it like a traditional shooter. You're better off making heavy use of your squad than pretending to be Rambo. The squad mechanics really make the game unique and fun.
The game hasn't aged as well as I had hoped. Graphically, it is inferior to Doom 3, which I believe is a year older. As far as gameplay, the squad AI, revolutionary for its time, still holds up relatively well. They only occasionally do very stupid things, ending with you dying. For instance, I was placing an explosive on a droid spawner, and a squad mate positioned to snipe shot me in the back four times. I had to be revived twice to finish the placement, and not a single droid hit me.
Besides the occasional annoyance, the squad is pretty intelligent and obedient. They are necessary, because the weapons in this game lack power. Enemies have a lot of health, and your guns do little damage. You'll quickly find yourself out of ammo without using a variety of weapons. Melee hits hard, but leaves you vulnerable. Melee is also a tad floaty, and it is easy to miss. In fact, aiming is far less responsive than in modern shooters. In short, the combat itself isn't overly impressive. It's functional, but that's it.
The audio is great. The music is as good as Star Wars always is, with plenty of familiar songs and some new. The voice acting is good for main characters, but some of the dialogue is pretty corny and often recycled. The characters are interesting enough for the length of the game.
This is a very linear game, all the way through, but I will never understand how this is a complaint about video games. I think it's just a word people like to throw around when they didn't enjoy a game, because they think it makes them sound smart. Some experiences are best left open-ended, but some are better being linear. This game would not benefit from the ability to aimlessly wander around and set your own path. It wouldn't even make sense in the context of being part of an elite commando squad. This game is linear, but it needed to be, and it doesn't ruin the experience in any way. If you want a non-linear game, there are literally hundreds to choose from. Stop demanding every game be non-linear.
As far as technical aspects, the game doesn't natively support higher fields of view and widescreen monitors. This can be fixed with some config file tweaking. I imagine it performs well on any modern hardware, seeing as how it is a decade old.
So basically, it's a good game, with some minor aging but more good than bad. Lasts about 6-8 hours.

Yes, the first few missions may be dull: Slice this, snipe that and so on. But that isn't the point. The point is, you need to work as a team. Sure, I may be a Star Wars fan myself but this doesn't affect my opinion on this fantasic game. To the people who say the graphics make up the game entirely, just do yourself a favour and don't play a single game for the rest of your life. Sure, the graphics in this game aren't up to scratch with today's standards but they sure were back in the good days of 2005. To be honest, I think they're great!
The gameplay and story line is simply amazing. It brings you back to Geonosis, Kashyyk, an abandoned Republic Cruiser and a few other places. I don't think there is another Commando game out there that is based on Star Wars. But if there is, this has got to be one of the best around. I spent heaps of time playing Star Wars Battlefront 1 & 2 and let me tell you, those are amazing games too. The squad that you play with is also very responsive and helpful (unlike in many other games). They'll do what you tell them to do. No questions asked. Unless they are under heavy fire and it is protocol-wise required to defeat the enemy first (goddammit just revive me already haha). Scorch really does keep the squad alive with his 'jokes', athough he can say it the wrong times.
But too bad Lucas Arts and Pandemic have left the Star Wars games, they were doing a fantastic job. Anyway, overall this is a fantastic game and I hope it won't be forgotten. If you are looking for a multiplayer, try going to Star Wars Battlefront 2. That is also an amazing game. I'll give it 9.5/10. Buy it already if you haven't! Have fun! :)

TLDR:
This game is pretty much the same as the first Magicka, but with some tweaks that make playing the game a lot more fluid.  I would say, mechanically, the game is better in every way save two:
- Can't pick up weapons and staves dropped by enemies
- Can't cast magicks as quickly as you input them
Mechanics aside, the game itself is really not better than the first Magicka in any way.
- Story is shorter and less interesting
- Enemies lack variety
- Bosses are easy
- Humor isn't very humorous
- Fights lack chaos (and opportunity to kill your friends)
- Spells feel balanced and boring
MORE DETAILS:
You can no longer pick up every weapon dropped by your slaughtered enemies.  Instead, the game has specific staff and weapon unlocks that you must discover as you play the game.  I feel this removes a big amount of variety that the first game had to offer, but the drawback is somewhat alleviated by the fact that you can choose your equipped weapon and staff from among those you unlock. This means you don't lose that awesome weapon you picked up from a boss a few levels back if you die, which is a great improvement over the first game.
The second mechanical drawback, which I absolutely hate, is that you can no longer cast magicks as quickly as you can input the elements.  My favorite magick to cast was Spike Quake: [s][s][d][s][s][space].  I can type that key combination very quickly, but, unlike the first Magicka, Magicka 2 forces you to wait a few seconds between casting, which is dumb.  This forces you to stand around and take damage while you wait for the game to let you cast your spells.
Magicka 2 seems to have gone for polish and balance over the first Magicka.  The polish is nice, but the balance just removes most of the aspects that made the first Magicka so enjoyable.  I'd recommend this game to anyone who has played the first Magicka and all the DLC and still wants more, or to anyone who hasn't played the first Magicka but likes the game's concept of casting spells and accidentally (or intentionally) killing your friends.  If you've played the first Magicka and have already had your fill of excitement, then you can probably skip this game.

The way Inexistence describes itself on the store page certainly makes it look appealing at first glance. A Metroidvania where we're a kid who maintains order and balance just by existing? Saving his sister (as opposed to a princess) from his older brother Claos by traveling through a vast world filled with varied places, mysteries, and action? I'm sold on just that it's a 2D Metroidvania.
Thing is, I wish Inexistence lived up to how it describes itself.
If by vast world you mean island with five destinations to travel to, you are correct. If by varied places you mean two houses with stretches of linear grassland that serve as tutorial places, a cave, a linear mountain pass, and a castle, you are correct.
Annex quests and hidden places? That one spot in each of the five areas you couldn't get to before because you didn't have one of the three acquirable skills yet.
Hald is as developed as the game sounds. Mash attack, or try to time it for a slightly faster (?) combo attack. Or just mash attack. You get the ability to use magic early on from Sahasrahla (yes, the exact name and essentially dude from Legend of Zelda: Link to the Past), but the damage is always inferior to the sword attack and the magic meter takes forever to recover.
Later on you get a double jump (complete with flapppy hands) and a teleport useful in all of five situations as it requires you to stand still and can only bring you across completely level terrain. Bumping the icon of where you're going to end up into something like stairs immediately fizzles the spell.
Four swords, four armors, four medallions, potions, antidotes (can't even remember being poisoned), and a couple  of key items are scattered around the Island. One medallion requires you collect seven golden puzzle pieces lifted straight out of Banjo-Kazooie.
I finished Inexistence to "100%" in 2 hours on Normal. Quotations because the game is bugged with regards to one of the boss fights in the Castle. Said bug messes with some of the treasure chests, forever screwing up your completion percentage and achievement gain for that saved file.
In between the stretches of "mash attack while you run forward", you get snipits of plot. Much of it never evolves beyond "Hald hates Claos and wants to defeat him because he's a hero". Then you whoop Claos'♥♥♥♥♥through all three final boss forms, and are given a whiplash twist ending. Ain't gonna spoil it, but it's the one thing the game made me feel something other than boredom (specifically confusion and discomfort).
If none of this scared you away like it should have scared me away, then worry not. 2016 winter sale it was marked down to 50 cents which, considering what I received and played through, isn't a bad deal. It's just 2 hours I'd have rather put into something else. Shame, considering the initial description and pixel art.
It's ironic to call Inexistence by that: absence of existence. 'Cuz there's an absence of a far better game than what we have, and I wish it could have been better.

With bland combat that doesn't offer a lot of attack/defense options, pushover boss-fights that go down on your first or second try, and have attack patterns you can memorize after seeing them once, Inexistence just sort of left a bad taste in my mouth. It's short, and I'm not really sure why there's an equipment system in the first place considering there's not that much equipment to obtain. Items might as well have been out the window as well, because there's two or maybe three you can use, and not once did I have to use an antidote because I never got poisoned. The game has some very interesting spritework, and at a glance it looks like it might be an impressive experience, but it's short, the enemies are predictable, the combat is bland, and the story is well. There's a twist at the end of the story that is one of the most bland and tasteless twists you can possibly make in a story. I suppose it's supposed to be evocative or shocking, but all it did was make me roll my eyes. Pass this one up. You'll just disappoint yourself.

Won my affections despite some serious flaws. Let me start with what is bad about this game. First, the story wanders all over the place and about 1/2 half of it could have been cut without any serious damage to the plot. Further, while there is a villian in the game he gets no character development. Second, the game relies on too many puzzles that are tedious--there is a place in the game where a written confession is needed and there are ten steps required to make the confession from producing the ink to getting a writing insturment. It takes a certain degree of patience to make it through Captain Morgane. My own strategy was when I found the game boring I started looking at a walkthrough until  the game seemed to pick up speed.
So what is good about the game? First, although the story wanders it does feature some nice plot twists. There is a genuine sense of adventure and of the unexpected. Second, the game flashes some moments of genuine humor. I won't spoil all of them but I'll mention one snarky bit, "She had the type of face that lauched a 1000 ships. That's why it looked so battered." ZING. There is even a Star Trek reference. Third, some of the characters one meets in the game are well-defined. The heroine of the game--Captain Morgane--is well-crafted as well as some of the minor characters. Finally, the game is nice to look at.
Overall, I found playing this game fun. True it doesn't rival Broken Sword or The Longest Journey but it's still is an above average adventure game. It took me about nine hours to finish and I don't regret the time spent.

I like survival games, and I love zombie games.  And this is definately a Survival zombie game.

See a group of 15 zombies?  toss a molly at them, burn them down and watch a new horde of zombies spawn in their ashes.  In an empty field?
