Distinctive art. Okay, it's not the prettiest, but I've played other games which used a lot more pixels to make boring art. Still, I do wish they'd put a tiny bit more effort into the "animations", especially for falling over.
Fair death system. Yes you can die, but the game saves for you, so you won't lose progress if you forget to save before "accidentally" blowing up the space station you're standing in.
If you're a fan of adventure games, Bik is well worth your time.

last year I played this after release with great anticipation expecting more ridiculous, overpowered spell fun with my friends and unfortunately this game fell leauges short of its predecessor. I dearly hope that the complaints I have and those from other players are given consideration here, we all would hate to see what could have been a game that could have surpassed the original Magicka go the way of Leviathan: Warships, dropped like a hot brick.

The reason why I bought this, and not other recording softwares like Bandicam, is for one, simple reason.
What happens when you go ahead and buy a program for a computer? Usually, it sticks to the computer's hard drive. This does have it's problems, though. If you switch between computers often, you will find out that you need 2 versions of the program for each computer, making it cost more. Minecraft has got this down; simply make an account and buy premium, and then the launcher is free. Steam is the same way, too. Although this type of program is only going to be used on 1 computer, what happens if your computer gets a virus, or your 8-year old son thought it would be funny to drop their dad's fragile gaming laptop/desktop off the top of the house. Well, you want to be prepared for those moments, and not be shot out of $XX for the programs on your computer.
First of all, LiteCam is only $10 cheaper. It's not alot, but $10 can be put somewhere where you want it more, like more strange killstreaks from TF2. And I've used the Bandicam Trial version and this version, and they are pretty neck-and-neck in quality. It also has some features that people can enjoy, but don't want to spend 100's of dollars on video editing software. Features like logo placement, video cam, and other things. Quality is pretty nice, I recorded about 45 minutes of footage for a YouTube video, and it looked pretty good.
Now, for the bad stuff. To start off, the video cam placement you choose doesn't matter at all, it's still going to be fullscreening the camera. Maybe I'm doing something wrong, but I've tried everything and it won't work. Second, if you want an easy-to-read FPS counter, you are in the wrong place. The FPS number is very small. Didn't really bother me, but may bother some others.
Next up, is not really the problem with this program, but with the Steam intergration. When liteCam crashes, which is uncommon depending on the situation, Steam still thinks I have it launched, when I don't. This is a problem when it comes to launch the recorder again, or when you want to sign out. You have to "wait" for liteCam to "close". It just ends up with me signing out of my computer and signing back in, and it works for me. Next, probably the biggest grip anyone else has, is the screen recording function. I've heard that it isn't good for anything at all. Personally, I haven't tried it yet, since I don't play browser games that much, even less for recording now. Bandicam has it covered there, unless if you want to pay $40 for each computer to use it. Your choice.
Lastly, they added in a video converter. This alone would be nice, but it stops there. Converting anything messes up with the audio, and it gives it this stupid distortion. If you need to convert, I have had good luck with Any Video Converter. It's free, and you can do all of the converting offline if you have to. It's also just good for everyday use.
All in all, for $30, it is a bit steep for what you are getting from other's viewpoints, but this is a license they are giving you to use this recorder. You can get payed on YouTube using this. And the toys they give you to edit your recording is nice, haven't seen that in Bandicam at all.
9/10. More features than seen in Bandicam, but screen recording, bugs with Steam, and other things keep this from being perfect.

I met one or two people who worked on the art of this game and kept meaning to get around to trying it so I really, _really_ wanted to like it, and may try more to check the DLC content or out of masochism, but seriously the base game is unbelievably annoying due to various bugs, trash filler content, BS design decisions, and complete unfriendliness to just trying the game out and exploring.  It doesn't look bad for a lower budget game so I guess the art people did do their part, but the rest of this game has too much downside.  I can't believe are still like this almost 3 years after release.
TL;DR = don't buy this game but I found it so annoying after while I am dropping a text wall here.
Here is a *not even complete* list of annoying crap from the base game:
Dumb friendly AI:
- Ally NPCs can provide backup, unless they randomly decide to leave you.  They also tend to leave at the start of difficult fights and mission sections with no warning or easy rule for all circumstances.
- Ally NPCs are often dumb as stones.  Sometimes during fights/sieges you have to put yourself at high risk because they are so stupid the will do nothing but continuously board up a window/etc.
Engine/physics problems:
- Characters glitch into geometry.  Zombies glitch in geometry.  Occasionally this will screw you and/or a mission hard.
- Climbing and jumping mechanics are sometimes crap.  Characters can get stuck on seemingly trivial objects/inclines, and can climb up certain objects which for some reason they cant climb down without taking damage (ladders work, but things like rocks do not).  Also when trying to jump down some areas you will "slide" in the air causing a farther fall and damage.  Sometimes will  also slide/fall off platforms when there is no reason, or fail to attach to a ladder when climbing down from something.
- Cars sometimes flip from almost nothing.  Once I flipped by turning ~10 degrees not even going fast.  Another time I bumped into a zombie going ~5mph in a parking lot.
Garbage design choices:
*** No way manually save/reload.  This is ridiculous in general and total garbage when trying to learn.  Something really bad happen?  Made any mistake?  Now choose between the hours or days to redo everything or carry on screwed over often due to some game glitch (loved losing the main character almost fully leveled because a horde is glitching stuck on a cliff next to a feral I can't stealth past and oh look my dumbass NPC ally left me on a mission suddenly 10x harder than any surrounding content). Why not have a noob mode/story mode and a hardcore mode (and for such a trivial developer task...)?  "Authenticity" can go to hell (and there are already so many super-unrealistic aspects of this game). I'd prefer the thing called “fun.”  This single feature would lessen or negate all other bugs and aggravations but obviously some designer thought they knew better and wasting your time was OK with them.  Unbelievably stupid and worse than anything on this list my a mile.
- No “pause” feature while trying to read UI options or journal entries.
- No way to turn off AFK progression.  This is especially annoying if you are essentially forced to AFK/quit for a while to rest characters.  It is also just incredibly annoying in general.  Oh look bad things happened when you went to work or tried to have a life.
- Very little explanation of what to do in the game past the most basic mechanics.  You learn mainly by trial and error and being forced to read online resources.  See also: no save/load errors--> massive waste of time to restart.
Time wasting filler design:
- The most interesting missions are probably story lines, at least to a newer player.  Except they are hard to get to because 99% of your time ends up devoted to the massive spamming of mundane threats and trash missions for lost/angry/depressed/sick/whatever NPCs so you will waste hours running the same crap over and over until you have a window.  Or you can just do them and risk ???/deaths by ignoring other tasks.  None of them show at all how important they are, what their time limit is, what consequences might be, if they are main missions or optional (though the standard spam ones become more obvious after a wile), etc. etc. etc..
- Zombies sometimes regenerate stupidly fast even in non-infested  areas/houses sometimes making gameplay super tedious.  Have had missions next to random houses before where new crops spawn every 2 minutes forcing you to fight endless trash mobs and making near zero progress.
- You take forever just to search a shelf, or can do it faster at risk of opening a black hole out of which zombies pour.  It's super fun searching slowly after hundreds of times.
- Even the healthy characters have some of the worst run/jog endurance ever making travel on foot super slow and annoying.
- You can carry several large objects/weapons, but 3 twinkies or bottles of aspiring apparently take up the same space.
- Searched objects don't retain highlighting so if you leave anything behind ever and want it later you have to manually hunt and peck to find storage.
UI:
- Controls don't handle very well and mouse aim works different than most action games which is annoying (affects move direction but not attack direction).  Attempts to aim in crowded melee combat are garbage.
- Hard to find relevant notices/mission text in journal list of everything from gain +1 to X skill or “bob took a dump +5 influence” and “bob accidentally shot bill in the face for no reason for the second time today -1 influence.”  Plus the game basically penalizes you for any trying to read these thoroughly (see: no pausing).

You will enjoy this game for at least 10 hours I assume.  After that you be wondering how this amazing game got so lost.
Lets start with the good:
-Graphics are well done, buildings and houses and car mechanics all great.
-It's a sandbox game and has base building.
-Game controls are fairly easy to use and generally work well.
-"Zombies" are realistic and can have a slight jump factor.
CONS:
-Gets old fast.
-you will constantly be having to go out and rescue people that wander off your base or be forced to settle disputes within your people almost constanty.
-You can never have more than one person with you at a time except for very limited "quest" circumstances.
-Resources are not infinite and neither are cars "although they can be fixed".
-"Special Zombies" can be tough at times.. you come out of a house and haven't saved in awhile and one of the huge zombies kills you.. well you're dead and that's it.  You just lost that person that you could have had since day one and was your best player.
-WHEN YOU LOG OUT THE GAME KEEPS PLAYING... so when you log back in some people could be gone or heaven forbid dead and your resources will be gone just about.  The longer you are logged out for the worse it is.
-Story is hardly worth bothering with.. it's mundane at best.
How this game should be:
-Open world sandbox.
-Single player good story.
-YOU pick the teams that go out and scavenge for food and tell them where and when to go.
-Make parties bigger than just a small group of 2.
-get rid of all the annoying distress signals "your people only leave the base if you tell them to"
-Need more materials in more places so you can play longer.
-Have more freedom on basebuilding and job assignments.
Do I think you wil enjoy this game? Sure but there is no way I can recommend this game for 30$ wait till it is 75% off before you even think about it.  I wanted to love this game.. sad.. really dissapointed stupid distress signals.. completely ruin the game.

Where do I even begin with this game. First off ive been playing this game for about 7 years now and every playthrough ive had of it was exellent. There is alot of variety when it comes to builds. There is the obvious Light/Dark or Grey option for the game but there is also Force user builds, Ranged builds, Pure combat focused guardian, etc. I find the combat to be enjoyable (In my opinion) since its tactical and you can really plan attacks and things of that sort. Take DA:0 for example. Its pretty much the same system. You can start with 3 beginning classes: Guardian (Combat focused), Sentinel (Better skill progression), and Consular (Force powers). You then later in the game get different set of prestige classes depending on your allignment. Now, lets get to the writing of the game. This game has one of the best stories I have ever seen. You'll see once you play it for yourself. The reason I prefer this game slightly over the first is just because I prefer the darker, philosophical, grey aspects of the atmosphere and story a bit better (Kotor 1 is also one of my favorite games). Anyways, this game presents the idea that Dark is not necessarily evil and Light isnt nessesary good and you really get to see the Flaws of both sides. For example, you play as the Jedi Exile, who was exiled from the Jedi order for rusing to war to protect innocents. The Jedi were lazy and waited to "evaluate the threat". The dialouge and voice acting in this game is absolutely fantastic (Especially Kreia). For this game, you dont even need to be a fan of Star Wars. A non Star Wars fan would look at this game and just play an RPG. However a Star Wars fan would look at this and play an amazing Star Wars RPG. The reason for this is because the game is set in an era wayyy before the Movies. One flaw however, would be the cut content presented this game. Obsidian (The developers) were rushed to release this game by lucasarts, resulting in them needing to cut out content for the game. Luckily, a group of community modders managed to get into the games files and restore alot of the content that was cut. You can find the mod on the steam workshop. Anyways, hurry up and buy the game! You wont be dissapointed.

Bik is an all-around wonderful point-and-click adventure. The art has both a retro and unique feel to it, complemented nicely by the music and sound effects. The story is engaging and the dialog is pretty funny. I laughed out loud several times throughout playing this. The gameplay is also really enjoyable. The scenes and puzzles vary from start to finish so it never feels stale.
What makes this game stand out from other point-and-click adventures is how it avoids tedium. You can highlight clickable items on the screen so that you're not just clicking everywhere all the time. Also, it's not possible to use every item in your inventory with everything on the screen. When you're trying to solve puzzles, many items will be greyed out for whatever object you're looking at. Now it's still possible to use the wrong item at times, the game doesn't just give you the answers, but this saves a lot of time that's normally spent trying every item combination in hopes of unlocking something. Best of all, despite these omissions, it still takes a long time to beat the game. This is a testament to how much actual content there is. By the end you'll really feel like you've been on a space adventure!
This is a fun game with a lot of charm to it. It's strange that this seems to have gotten no attention on Steam. It's one of the better point-and-click adventures out there and I recommend it to anyone who's even a casual fan of the genre.

This was my favourite game for a while (the low play time is because I used to have a non-Steam version).
I'm not going to pretend it's perfect, but it is definitely worth playing. It presents itself as a tactical squad-based shooter, and it fills that role pretty well. Experienced FPS players may be able to get by without squad support, but there are bits where they are very useful, if not necessary. Their AI is capable, though occasionally will do stupid things.
The selection of weapons is decent. There are a variety of generic sci-fi FPS guns, as well as some typical Star Wars weapons, like the bowcaster. For the most part they have a decent 'feel' to them (you feel like you're hitting something, unlike in, say, Battlefront, where all the weapons have no recoil).
One of the best things, though, is the setting.  This is a grittier take on the Clone Wars, with no Jedi jumping around and doing Force-magic. You play as the leader of an elite commando squad, with beefier armour and better weapons than the average clone. The settings are very atmospheric and well-animated, particularly Kashyyyk. One thing that really stands out, however, is the UI and sound design. You see the world through your character's visor, which has nice touches like an electric wiper to clean off droid oil or bug blood. The sound quality of your character's voice really makes it feel like you're wearing a helmet.
All in all, it's a sound sci-fi shooter, and the biggest shame is that it wasn't longer, and that there was no sequel, especially given the twist at the end. I suspect the multiplayer is also passable if you have friends who also have the game, but I've never played it more than 1-on-1.

It's bloody, gritty and rather tricky. A Star Wars game for a more mature demographic with likable characters with, albeit cliched, personalities.
You got your rough and tumble borderline serial killer 07 - Sev
You got the fun and dumb but highly trained demolitionist 62 - Scorch
You got the bottom feeding, intellegent and downright square 40 - Fixer
Then there's you, the quick thinking leader of Delta Squad - 38 - Boss
They may have differing personalities and prefernces but at the end of the day each sqaud member is very copy and paste in terms of usefulness and each one gets the job regardless of what they prefer to do which is good, why leave a Commando half cooked?
The gameplay aspect was astounding. The Ai are intellegent (bar some hiccups) and follow orders very well. You say 'Search and Destory' they'll take point and peek around corners before engaging the enemy.
Say 'Group Up' and, well, they come to you like a Jack Russel that heard a bag open.
Give the order to 'Secure Location' and they actually dig in, taking cover behind objects and not leaving that spot unless you put them on a position but even if one goes the other two stay and keep digging in, its great if you need to heal at a bacta station under heaby fire.
Lastly there's the 'Move On' command which ends whatever action the commando's are doing and will either fall back to a secured location if a marker was placed or come back to you.
In battle you HAVE to be the leader. These guys wont do more than cover and shoot unless you point them towards a turret, sniper location or explosive ordinance spot. There's nothing finer than having all three squad mates on useful points as you go against a small army of droids. There are also non-combat meneuvers like Slicing a terminal, setting a detonator charge or Breaching and Clearing a room. Your surroundings are as much of a weapon as anything though, one part I liked was when I had my squad distract a heavily armoured spider droid while I snuck around the back, sliced a terminal and dropped a crate on its head.
Droids also have this annoying habit of being extremely hard to kill. Maybe the battle droids are easy but Super Battle Droids, Destroyer Droids and Spider Droids are tough and require you to focus the entire squads fire on one at a time. There are other enemy types but I wont spoil it.
All in all this is a fun game but with a sadly abrupt ending. It almost felt like they ran out of funding halfway through and ended it at the worst moment possible. I literally felt like someone came into my bedroom and pulled the blug on my PC, that was how abrupt the ending blackout was.
All in all you can get some 15-16 hours out of it which isn't too bad. It's a good game with solid FPS mechanics and some great voice acting where it counts and despite its abruptness the ending was fairly good and will leave you wanting more.
9/10 solid gameplay with very very few glitches but with an abrupt ending

For a game that is getting close to 20 years old, it has still held its own in most areas. I stumbled upon it a few days after it had come up on the Steam Store, I was looking for a free game that wasn’t too tasking on my friends’ school laptops, and I guess I struck gold!
This classic game is given a new breath of life. By being added on to the steam store Valve has done us the kindness of allowing maps from the original Half-Life game to be added to the already large selection of maps available. New players are flooding in by the hour to see what this classic has in store. I was surprised to see servers being hosted in Australia, for such an old game.
Although the game has visually aged pretty badly, graphics do little to deter the involving and tricky puzzles that lie in popular fan made maps. As such, it can be played on any computer, making it an available choice for both diehard fans of the half-life games as well as casual gamers who may not have the hardware to play the more complex games that the steam store has to offer. I for one, found it entertaining to see weapons and objects that were copied into early versions of Counter-Strike and Team Fortress Classic.
I was surprised to find that Sven has features that I believe are lacking critically in Garry’s Mod, a similar gen of game built off the much newer Half-Life 2 game. For example, the vote screen in SVEN to change the map or to kick/kill a player is brought up simply by pressing the letter ‘v’, while in GMOD; the player has to enter console commands to begin a vote.
A few very minor issues are that sometimes the voting screen doesn’t work so the user cannot select to kick players or change the map, or vote screens do not show up, so players cannot vote yes or no on a proposed action. On rare occasions I have found that maps can be a bit buggy, for example there are points in which we solve a puzzle which obviously is meant to open a door, but instead the door does not open. This could either be created by the map creator, or it could also be caused by new bugs created by updates in the game. One would think that these issues would have been fixed long ago, if not before the game was listed on the steam store, so players could experience a very nicely polished game upon release.
My next point is not an issue with the development, but more so the players that one is likely to find in the game, there is something of a communication issue between players when it comes to solving puzzles in the game, where more experienced players tend to rush through the map, as they know it inside out, leaving other players lost, or newer players having gone through half the map before another faster player has completed it, leaving newer players dissatisfied with their experience. The only thing that can be done to fix this is up to the players, to encourage use of the text and voice chat.
One of my favourite moments in the game was an hour or two into the game, when I called for first aid on a full server. I was promptly trapped in the middle of five to seven other players, who then began to heal each other as well as myself until everyone was at full health… Then we got run over by a player who was driving the train for the first time. It just goes to show that although not everyone knows how to complete the map, everyone knows how to heal a player in need.
The one piece of advice I have for new players is to choose your skin and online name before you join a server, unless you want to cop flak from more seasoned players. After all, who wants five ‘New Player’ Freemans jumping around in a server?

I had lost faith in point-and-click adventure games during the last months. I kept on buying them, some even blindly, because I wanted them to be good. But they rarely even met the standards of the 90s games they tried to emulate.
, on the other hand, is a great game. I mean, a proper one.
It contains timed passages. Deaths are frequent, but never unfair (the game always autosaves beforehand). I just fought some sort of boss, I could move freely and shoot it with my blaster. It still is a classic adventure game, not a hybrid, but developer Zotnip knows this genre is about letting people DO things, not restricting them.
Think of
, a game where you could switch on your TV - in almost every other adventure, TVs are always broken or the main character doesn't want to watch.
In
, you're constantly asked to handle situations, fix things, work something out. And because everything is fast - no painful, slow dialogue, fadeouts, dragged-down-by-Unity interfaces - you're never punished for trying things out.
Now, for the presentation. People call this game ugly, done with MS Paint and so on. Maybe, as a fan of reduced EGA-type graphics in general and titles like
my opinion isn't that valid, but ...
I'm glad about every developer breaking the mold. Here, it's more about perspective and grain than choice of colours, since the cyan magenta-thing isn't that new. Sure, there are traces of
and
in
, but please, why call it ugly? It's bold.
Sure, Wadjet Eye Games for example do their thing very well, but they're are also stuck in some conservative 90s with benefits limbo. They are miles away from having a style you could call "distinct".
It is obvious that each screen has been composed with lots of care, neither too empty, nor too cluttered and I find that very pleasing, except for some particle effects, which are really not very good.
The moody and well-produced music, by the way, is the best I've heard in this genre in a long time.

Exactly why this game is still in early access, I do not know. There is not a game in existence that has more depth and replayability than Factorio. With 0.15 it has become so configurable and moddable that you can turn it into several completely different games - make it as easy or as difficult as you want it to be or just completely overhaul the game mechanics.
You build factories - huge, self sustaining factories. You gather raw resources such as iron and copper (automated), process them into higher tier products (automated), turn those products into end products (automated) and use those end products to enlarge your factory (also automated with robots!), increase your research production, invent more epic equipment and ultimately rule the galaxy. No, not really although I'm sure there is a mod for it. You fire a rocket into outer space with a satellite in it, presumably to get in contact with your own kind. Nobody cares about why you launch the rocket, really. The better question is: how many can you launch at once before your computer can't handle it anymore?
The game tells you you've won when you launch a single rocket, but there is no stopping this game. You launch another rocket - you do it 10 more times. You fire a rocket a minute. 10 rockets a minute. Do you know how much iron you need mine to be able fire 10 rockets per minute? I don't know, but you alsways need more iron. Always more and more.
Or you start over and build bigger, use more trains, try to build as compact as possible, try to get the more impossible achievements (fire a rocket in under 8 hours... it's madness), build nuclear bombs and go to town on the natives - whatever your creative mind demands you to do. There are no limits to the number of challenges you can set for yourself in this game. Try a death world where you are literally boxed in by the hostile natives of the planet and need to fight for your life every step of the way (remember those nukes?).
Just be aware that this game is addictive and WILL cause the Tetris effect. It is not a joke, it is a reality for many people. But that's just the best thing ever because then we can play Factorio in our sleep as well. Did I say sleep? When was the last time I slept?

I saw that the reviews were getting better since the initial release so I decided to give it a try. While I'm happy that the AI's difficulty has been upped since the first game, I abhor the spell cooldown system. A huge part of my enjoyment while playing the first magicka was spamming overpowered spells after having memorised each and every one of them. With Magicka 2, you can no longer do that.
Other than that, the game has been really entertaining for me so far, the storyline, humor, even better than the first game. Would probably be more fun once I play this multiplayer.
Edited (After completing campaign on normal difficulty, attempting some trials and challenges on normal and hard difficulties and collecting all magicks):
It seems that the idea of having a cool down for spells is actually for balancing purposes. After getting used to the controls, I feel like normal mode is easy as long as you calmly analyse the enemies' elemental resistance and cast the appropriate elements countering them. It is no doubt more difficult than the first Magicka so take some time to learn the elemental and spell interaction mechanics. Moving around is much more important as shield spells are no longer as strong as they used to be. Ultimately, I think this is actually better than the first Magicka although I still find myself soloing most things since many people will immediately kick you from their game without even letting you show your abilities to work as a team without blowing them up to bits in every battle.
Verdict: Get this game, especially if you have good friends who can play with you. Seriously, like 9/10 rating, for its price this is one of the most enjoyable games I've had in a long time.

In what appears to be par for the Sniper Elite series, Nazi Zombie Army suffers from a notable lack of imagination.  Departing from even the regular series stream (which I actually prefer, and which I have enjoyed, as the 'sniper' designation fits those games very well), this is an almost entirely 'shoot em up' based game, which appears to ditch the sniper aspect of the series, referring you instead to level after level of 'survive this horde by blasting them away'.  There's such a serious lack of strategy here, that - after logging in about 5 hours total - I don't think I've been able to play through an entire round (of killing endless mobs of nearly identical enemies), without becoming strikingly bored and disinterested.  Much like the Dead Island series fell flat, and brought its share of disrepute to the zombie/undead game genre, this is a similarly forgettable addition to the zombie gaming series.  For future developers - the golden rule of content in gaming is; if you have nothing unique to add to a genre beyond a mildly entertaining shoot-em-up action game, then you'd best leave it to the developers who have real experience and expertise in the genre, instead of wading into an unfamiliar genre with mixed results at best.  Final verdict - this game is at the level of a free DLC, and little more.

And the 5 chapters which span out as 5 years of the player's life did give me a feeling of really experiencing time lapses by ending the previous chapter's conversation with a fade only to hear from Emily once again after a period of time, and it placed distance and uncertainty between Emily and the player, which is something that happens in life.
A lot of players don't recommend this game due to the depressing end, and the fact that there's no alternative 'happier' ending.
I liked the premise itself, and I do feel the execution could be better. Things like character development, the quality of the characters (Emily can sometimes be prone to guilt tripping you, and the communication between these two adolescents awaits improvement), the length of the game and the depth of their long term friendship.  But for what it's worth (free to play), and given the circumstances of the characters (less mature teenagers who are at the beginning of finding their stand in the world) it's done a pretty decent job at getting its idea across.
I can get how some would prefer having a happier ending. But I enjoy having some games like this that remind me things like this happen. You lose people, you grow apart from people, the bitter memories you have, the mistakes that you regret, life is depressing at times and it's perfectly fine.

Visuals: Terrible. Some games thrive from their simplicity by compensating with an amazing experience. There is no amazing experience here to make up for these simple geometric shapes scattered across a field.

And also anyone having problems with 1920x1080 resolution
1. Go to: Steam > Steamapps > Common > star wars republic commando > GameData > save > system.ini
2. Open system.ini and under [WinDrv.WindowsClient], change:
WindowedViewportX=1920
WindowedViewportY=1080
FullscreenViewportX=1920
FullscreenViewportY=1080
3. under [WinDrv.WindowsClient], find and change:
Bumpmapping=true to false
no more crash at new game and 1920x1080 resolution

This game is only slightly like the original. I can see they tried to make is more 'challenging', but in reality the only thing that makes is challenging is the lack of freedom the player has with the abilities themselves. Placing timers between casting the same spell, weakening shields so you're constantly spamming them just to stay alive, taking more damage from your own abilities, and making it so that elemental immunity requires 4 of one element+shield (Which effectively means you better pick one and take physical plus other elemental damage, or choose your poorly protective simple shield... in which you still take a considerable amount of health damage). In reality; the first game was fun because it was humorous, and had a sense of power for the player wherein you could spam spells as fast as your fingers could type them, and the enemies kept coming with different attributes, forcing creativity with a very intuitive and genius system. Taking away power from the player does not create a challenge, it creates frustration. I was very disappointed in this version of the game, and if I could I would ask for my money back. I plan to simply play expansions for the first one until I am done with them.

As I write this, the release date for GTA V is fast approaching. Hard to believe it's been 5 years since GTA4 was released.
GTA: Episodes from Liberty City (EFLC) moves the base GTA4 game forward nicely. There's two smaller storylines, each about 12-16 hours of gameplay. Both stories are interwoven with the main GTA4 storyline. Niko Bellic and other characters make appearances in these games, and certain loose ends are tied up in these episodes.
The stories are strong, the supporting characters are interesting, and the protagonists are fun to play. Luis Lopez, the main character in The Ballad of Gay Tony, is my new favorite GTA protagonist - even better than Vice City's Tommy Vercetti. These two smaller games are much more interesting to me than Niko Bellic's story.
EFLC delivers some technical fixes and gameplay improvements to the base game.  Most notably, we now have mid-mission checkpoints, so if you fail a mission, you can pick up part-way through. This really decreases the frustration level of the game. Less notably, but important to me: traffic is more realistic. And, motorcycles are easier to control.
The Ballad of Gay Tony is the standout episode. It brings back the over-the-top flavor of Vice City and San Andreas. The missions are crazy fun, including a shootout on top of the Empire State Building, hijacking a subway car, helicopter duels, and a race around Manhattan -- excuse me, "Algonquin" -- involving parachutes, speedboats and fast cars. There's a new cage-fighting mini-game, and everywhere you turn in this one, there's fast cars to boost. And, as mentioned, parachuting! There's 20 optional missions involving base jumping and parachuting skills. Excellent fun. The Ballad of Gay Tony pulls out all the stops to show off what this game engine is capable of delivering. And maybe, hopefully, it shows that Rockstar hasn't forgotten how to have fun.
If you need a GTA fix before GTA V appears and you skipped these episodes, you should definitely take a second look.

TL/DR at the bottom.
There is so many things to say about this game, I don't even know where to start. That's when I make a list to clarify my ideas, so here it goes.
Pros:
-Some devs like to keep their community informed, and then there's Wube Software. Just a quick look at ANY of the "Friday Facts" post that they do every Friday will tell you A LOT about the devs. They go in MANY details explaining what they are doing, so much so that anyone who would like to learn how to make a video game would be better off reading the Friday Facts here than spending the same amount of time watching tutorial videos on the internet.
-The game is a decent price and will never go on sale because the devs are confident enough in their product. that's refreshing, no more waiting for the next Steam sale and then hoping that your wishlist-games go on sale.
-The game has had a stellar ratio of positive to negative reviews. By stellar I mean that I'm pretty confident in saying that at any given time since launch it has been top 3 on Steam for the positive/negative ratio.
-The gameplay on the vanilla game offered me 126h51m25s of pure fun for my first complete run. That right there is already good enough for my taste but I can/will get more than 1,000 hours out of this game easily over the course of the next year or so because....
-There is a whole world of user-created mods to try out. I've installed Bob's mod, the most popular of them all afaik and I've managed to do what I'd consider to be half of the progress in a duo-coop game with a friend in a bit over 90 hours so I'm thinking if I was playing solo with the same mods it would take me around 360 hours to complete it.
-The game is still in early access with lots of content being added with every new version. Sometimes some of the modded content ends up inside the base game in the next version because the devs can recognize what works and what doesn't and they won't shy away from making their game the best they can.
-The music is great, I usually get tired of a game's music within 2 hours of playing it, unless it changes often (which is not the case in Factorio), but here the music fades away and comes back for brief periods of time, it's really not intrusive and adds to the mood instead of forcing the mood on the user.
Neutral: -The graphics are... how to put it... just look at the screenshots. When you are completely zoomed in it's pixelated, but then again you can't play the game zoomed in like that, more than likely you are zoomed out a whole lot most of the time you spend in the game. And when zoomed out a lot, the game starts to look like a circuit board. What I'm trying to say is, it's kinda block-ish. I guess you either like it or you don't. I have no problem with it but I suppose I'm putting this in the neutral points as I could see this being the only thing to turn off a potential player that made it as far as the review section, and as far into my review.
Cons: - This game will make you remember about all the other games you've ever played where you would say to yourself, very late at night: "ah damn, I'm just going to do one more [insert specific repeatable action here] before I go to bed." And then you'll tell yourself: "aaaaaaaw, isn't that cute, back then I thought I knew what it was to want to do "just one more..." Now I really need to finish this conveyer belt before I go to work because once again the sun has come up and I could have swore it was only 2am just 20 minutes ago!"
20 hours after starting to play the game I decided that as soon as I was done placing a particular conveyer belt I would come here and write a review. It seems to have taken me 338 more hours of play time to finally have the time to write a review. Not quite sure where all that time went, still feels like it was only 3-4 nights ago. Anyway I don't have time to look for all those hours of my life, I need to go defend my base, some aliens are mad at me for grabbing all of their iron ore.
Final words: The game will never go on sale so you might as well buy it now if you made it all the way through my review (because I'm sure that if you haven't been turned off yet then this game is for you).
TL/DR: No micro-transactions, no DLCs, best steam reviews ratio, awesome gameplay, runs on low-end computers just fine, great replayability with user-created mods, moody atmosphere, and you get to kill aliens with a flamethrower.

-weapons feel underpowered compared to how they look in the movies and shows like Clone Wars or Rebels\

NOTE: READ BEFORE DISLIKING THE REVIEW.
Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army is the spin off series where you don't fight soldiers, but instead you fight Nazi Zombies. Will you want to play this game or will you want to stick to the originals ?
Story wise there's not much story at all. You can play up to 4 different characters who have to escape Berlin which is filled with Zombies Hitler woke up from the dead, it's just absurd as it sounds.
Gameplay wise it's an identical re skin of Sniper Elite V2. Nothing is changed. The game now focuses on close quarters combat. Trust me when I say this. It's not fun when a horde of zombies gang up and try to kill you and the only thing you have to defend yourself with is a sniper rifle. The are two types of boss battles. One is a big guy zombie who was  a machine gun and it's best to snipe him from afar and there is a poltergeist type boss which can spawn enemies in the area you are fighting in.
Music is alright for the most part. It feels like a great reference to 80's horror movies and a throwback to classic zombie flicks.
Graphics wise, it's an identical clone to Sniper Elite V2. Even some of the levels are ripped straight from V2. All that is changed is that all levels take place during the night and it has this weird greenish filter on top of it.
The game took me 6 hours to finish the entire campaign in Co Op mode.  There is some replay value if you want to find hidden collectibles. Otherwise there is zero replay value.
The game is pretty difficult due to the unfair nature of the enemy placement. I will refer to one of the experiences I had while playing the game. During the 4th mission of the game right before the end of the mission I had to go through a closed door. As soon as I opened it I got downed instantly by 7 zombies before I could even react. Not to mention if you play Co Op you have less checkpoints and if you ♥♥♥♥ up you might have to redo entire sections of a level to get back to the part where you failed.
Level Design is alright for the most part. Some levels have massive open area's in which it's hard to get swarmed which is nice.
The game is incredibly buggy. I had ton's of bugs during the time I played the game. Like enemies glitching through walls. The game not letting me pick up items and more stuff like that.
Overall I wish there was a middle option for this game, cause while I don't find it completely horrible, I don't find it good either. It get's boring really soon and there's a lot wrong with the game. In the end this game is made only for the massive fans of Sniper Elite games. If you are a fan of the Sniper Elite games you will love this game. But I still suggest waiting for a discount before buying this game. I give Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Army a 5/10

This is a typical "console shooter". You go from one beautiful location to the next following a narrow path through carefully orchestrated sequences of enemies popping out at the exact same time as you happen to get there. You are often led to believe that you have actual tactical choices but in reality everything boils down to "go slow and be careful". Your fellow AI team members add great atmosphere, and the game would not be the same without them, even if their only tactical value is to provide clues about how far you got in the scripted sequences (they almost always wait to advance until you cleared the next wave of enemies, for example). According to the game itself, the easiest difficulty level is for "content tourists". IMO this label applies to the whole (single player) game no matter the difficulty level.

This is from my personal experience.
I have been using this software for a few months now and between multiple computers,
(Two gaming computers, one being high end, one being a medium end gaming rig, and my non-gaming laptop.)
From all 3 of these computers I've used the program on I've only had 1 single problem with this software when I had first purchased it, which was it crashed from alt - tabbing in a game, and kept crashing till I re-installed it, after that it works fine.
From my main computer (high end rig) |
I've been able to max this program out to what I deam an acceptable recording software, and was able to record with absolutely zero frame loss at 100fps setting, personally I haven't left the software with the No limit setting, simply because there was no reason to even record over 100 fps.
From my secondary old computer (medium end rig) |
I was able to once again max this program out to what I wanted and still using the 100 fps recording settings. The only minor setback was it would drop my fps by about 6 from what I had personally capped it at in my games. Keep in mind though I had this computer for around 3 years already and was running some outdated badly bugged hardware... yes I know, shame, yeah, yeah.
From my non-gaming laptop |
I was able to set the program to record 40fps without much stuttering between frame capture and playback. Though this is with a cheapy $300 laptop I bought for working on a year before.

Now that the original version of State of Decay is not available on Steam Store any more, it no longer makes sense to me to compare the two versions and try to make your point pro or against upgrading to YOSE. So, I deleted my previous review and wrote a new and more general one instead, mainly for those who are not yet familiar with State of Decay at all.
EDIT: The DLCs are still available for the original version, but the main game is not.
In my opinion, this is quite an underrated game in general, and to me the best zombie game I have purchased so far. I can't say that I'm a huge fan of the genre and have tried even nearly them all, but I have seen my share of gameplay for quite a few of them. Anyway, I feel that the user review aggregate doesn't do State of Decay itself as a game any justice, because of the controversy the YOSE edition caused with it's pricing weighed against it's added content which many felt was next to nonexistent.
First of all, I really like the combat system that actually has more depth to it than at first meets the eye. The variety of different melee and ranged weapons and the personal skills and abilities of different individuals make many different character builds viable and add to the replay value. The range of weapons is nicely complemented by the crafting possibilities of different explosive and incendiary weapons for horde control. Not to mention the use of different vehicles not only as a means of transport, but also as a quick and relatively safe way of  thinning out the densest ranks of zombies.
Yet the most compelling point to me is the importance of scavenging and resource management, which with different home base upgrades adds a strategic aspect to the game. Where to build your outposts, what resources to stack and how to best put them to use are questions you have to constantly ponder to best suit your preferred way of surviving. Chance also plays a role here as the composition of your group of survivors, their traits and proficiencies have an effect on which may be the most beneficial way to go on each playthrough.
I highly recommend this one to anyone who doesn't mind a bit of thinking and planning in addition of the merciless slaughter of the undead.

I played a non-Steam version of this game for an hour and then decided it wasn't just that I was experiencing this Trip for free. [Insert Drug Dealer Joke]
The game is a walking simulator. The pull is the world. The gamer-oriented object (thus far) is to collect sprites.
I qualify that last point thusly because the dev has expressed that the intent IS more of an [footnote] interactive art installation [end footnote], rather than a trippy "game," per se.
I have heard, however, that the dev is seriously considering tweaking the vision into a form more akin to "game" - what I've heard suggested that it might become something like Pokemon Snap. Research and observe the structures and creatures; use a camera and take notes.
There is currently no music.
There are too many invisible walls.
The lack of a sprint is to the players' advantage (more time to explore); however, I think different means of locomotion might add to the experience. Crawl, slither, fly - whatever.
Just give us some curve balls that will provoke further "Woah"'s.
If the screenshots interest in any way - If "walking simulator" isn't a bad word to you.
There should be no hesitation to Trip.
[footnote] From the few posts I've read pertaining to Trip: Steam Edition, the players complain about that lack of interactivity. You truly do just walk around, marvel at the sights and collect those sprites, should you find them. As a free non-Steam game, that's not really a valid complaint; it's being called a game is not called into question because there IS some sort of interactivity. A free trip to a fantastic virtual world.
With it being sold for money, of course people will expect more. In general, from what I've seen, walking simulators that live up to the name usually have Mixed user ratings. But. Those that have a gimmick are more well-received.
The Stanley Parable; truly a walking simulator. Due to it being so unique, the positive reviews outweight the negative.
With Trip, the uniqueness is strictly in the visuals. There are other comparable games to it, like FRACT OSC and NaissanceE and Kairo - these are first-person puzzlers with an abstract style.
Trip is all about the abstract.
Might seem like I'm subverting my recommendation with this cyclical talk, but I contest that Trip is worthy of patronage, so as to further fuel the vision, whatever it amounts to. Personally, more of the same with no further "gamey" mechanics implemented would be fine; I would then hope for an open world, but...
I just want this game to succeed; at least as a walking simulator, (I think) it has more substance than most... my saying so challenges the definition of "substance," but the abstract has that effect.

I love  psychedelia, either in   music,  art or playing psychedelic looking games, unfortunately I was quite disappointed in TRIP: Steam Edition after experiencing it  for nearly 10 hours in bite-sized chunks over the last 24 hours since I purchased it; that is,  at least in its present state.  As it is early access I may change my  opinion  as time progresses, but that will depnd on what the developer does for the game.    It says the artware  is an open world  environment;  for me that conjures up   the thought that you are able to explore every part of the  world you find yourself in. Sadly  I found there were many places I wasn't able to explore, for example  trying to  get   from many places   via hills, you aren't able to climb anything steeper than about 45 degrees, this  basically locks off  loads of  area of the world so far created.  I tried for hours to find ways to access  certain area's, but   was always held back by the inability to climb anything too steep.
The actual  artware/game (I include game because  Steam imply that its also a game  when it asks the question,   'Approximately how long will this game be in Early Access?') is basically an exploration game, nothing else, just wandering around looking at the weird  shapes and colors.  For  several minutes I found this  quite exciting and stimulating, but  eventually  found it a little bit too much  after  an hour of wandering around.   I was determined to contine, but had to break the experience up into  chunks.
I know the developer has said they intend expanding the game and adding different worlds.  I'm sure   those additions will add a little more interest.  also they said    that  the game was a  visually tantalizing open world artware that culminates the player to relax and enjoy a safe enviroment for them to explore at their own pace and that there are no objectives, no rules, just beauty and art.  Yes, I can agree with that, it  does   definitely help you to relax, but   why are we calling it a game , or   more  truthfully  selling it as a game.  As a piece of experimental  artware, I'd be happy, but I  wanted a game..  Okay, I read the  description and still purchased the 'artware'.  Still I wasn't expecting it to   be so tedious.  Lets hope the additional content the developer has promised will  materialize and expand on what's already here and in fact evolve it into more than just artware; lets see an artware based game  with  some substance to it.
for example:
I really think think  the game/artware  needs a little more than just  more places to explore.  We need   some incentives to carry on exploring the world; maybe some  puzzles to unlock hidden area's, mini games,  or even a mode  that allows   some sort of co-operative play or PvP.  These would certainly add interest and  IMO would  increase  the  numbers buying this game   three fold or more.
Thankfully the price of the game even without the   initial release  discount  is quite cheap at £4.49 (probably even cheaper in the US), but, unless you really like   games with little content apart from weird, colorful  and pretty visuals, I'd steer clear unless it goes on sale or   the developer   adds some thing more to do  apart from wandering around.  To be honest, I can't believe I've spent 10 hours on this game.  (Maybe   I was enjoying myself so much i didn't realize the time, though it's more likley I fell asleep at times at  the keyboard.  :)
To the developer.  If you do read this,  I'd like to say, I really want to like this game,  the color palette you've used is excellent, the visuals are pretty awesome  and the game has loads of potential, but  please please please  add some  content (some examples quoted above)  that gives the player an incentive to carry  on playing, or at least add  the ability to interact with other players or NPC's, maybe  make the odd characters and animals (eg the camel) that I found in game  actually  animated rather than just statuesque.  I really did loved  the   visuals and look forwards to seeing more, but I can't recommend this to my friends as it stands.

Campfire Cooking is a must have for puzzle game fans. Everything about this game is very polished, from the visuals to the cute story to the masterful level design. The game mechanics are very simple, you can only push, pull, slide your stick to the side and sometimes rotate a stick. But from the ingenious level design these simple mechanics can lead to some very satisfying and challenging levels.
The game is split up into different areas, each introducing a new gameplay element and aesthetic. The level difficulty has a nice ramp up until you reach the final area which acts as one last test for everything you've learned thus far. The levels in the last area are truly challenging and this world has many of my favorite levels in the game. If you manage to beat all 100 levels, you'll be awarded with 5 expert levels that live up to their name.
For only $6 this game is definitely worth your money and your time. I highly recommend Campfire Cooking!

First off, some fo the good things:
The graphics look absolutely gorgeous, multiplayer has FINALLY had the fix the entire community was waiting for in that you can now add players in the middle of a level, there are some new magicks and the boss fight mechanics are new and challenging in most cases.
So why do I not recommend this game?
In short: it's boring. Don't get me wrong, the chaos is still a lot of fun, but it doesn't really change, the story is virtually nonexistent, and it is so obviously intended for people who have already played magicka 1, yet it fails EXACTLY to bring that one thing magicka 1 players have been waiting for for years: something new.
Magicka 2 is simply another expansion to the original game with slightly altered game mechanics and improved graphics. To be totally honest, I find presenting it as a whole new game a form of rudeness.
I mean, sure, it has a lot of humour, but there is a problem with that as well:
In most games, it is fun to find the occasional easter egg and laugh about it. In THIS game, there is so much humour around every corner and under every stone that it feels like the makers tried to conceal the lack of story with a boatload of cheap humour. In my honest opinion Seitokai no Ichizon had less reference jokes than this game.
In short: if feel to me like the purpose of this game was not to bring a new and original challenge, not to please the dedicated fans, not to broaden the game's audiance by making a wholly new game from it (because with the amount of bugs in Magicka 1 a wholly new game was much needed)(not that this game is free of bugs, though it has considerably less), it feels like the purpose was to appeal to an audiance as broad as possible in order to rake in as much money as possible. They got me hook, line and sinker, but I have 9 hours in this game and I finished all relevant parts of it.
And the extra content? Costs more money. Sorry Paradox but this is not what I paid for.

Magicka 2 is a Comedy, Action, Adventure Co-op game and, I don't know why the reviews are at mixed. The game is fantastic, and a great prequeal to Magicka.
In Magicka 2, you need to save a prophesized child, Lok, from the Orks. To do that, you must find and use a spell that not even Lok can defeat, to weaken her, so that you can take her safely, so that the Orks don't get her first. It is a really great game, and the Co-op is good as well. For anyone who has played Sanctum 2, Magicka 2's Co-op is similar to Sanctum 2's. You can make a public, friends only, or private server. A public server means that anyone, anywhere can join, which can be helpful. The other two modes are self explanitory. The spell system is similar to Magicka's. But, the weapon system is different, for each staff and melee weapon you find, will be saved to your inventory at the main menu. Same thing with robes.
Overall, this is a really fun game, and I was shocked to see it at mixed reviews. However, I can see why people didn't really like this game. It does, yes, feel more like a prequeal to Magicka: Wizard Wars than to the first Magicka. However, I do recommend this game to everybody, because, despite the reviews, this is a really good game.

I've really only begun the game and I've found myself charging into enemies headfirst, where in the original my character would stay rooted and be able to focus on casting, Having to manage my character from charging off into enemies faces to get melted is a frustration I'm finding bringing me out of the experience.
I don't mind not being able to move my character while casting, if it means I can focus on slaming out the spell on my keys and not having to worry about galavanting off into enemy fire.
Another instance of this has been my attempts to cross water by freezing it, only then to slip off the edge and die because I'm focused on the casting of the spell. This has occured even while using the binded "stop" key.
However, to be fair, I did go into the settings and change around a few keybindings to attempt to replicate the feeling I had while playing the original Magicka. The game feels great for that part, but the movement while casting has ruined it for me personally.
Oh, as I also found out the hard way, wards don't exactly work anymore. For example, casting shield and water doesn't prevent you from getting wet like it does in the original Magicka.
I suppose, in the end, I was really hoping for a continuation of the style in the original Magicka.

Before reading this review I want to start off by saying that it's not a bad game. However as time passes things become outdated. This is one such thing.
Gameplay
It's a standard battlefield game. It has 4 classes recon, medic, engineer and assult. Each class has a vareity off weapons to choose from and different abilities. It's a very fun game and it can lead you to the top of your seat as you rush into battle.
There are also several different gamemodes conquest, rush, squad rush and squad deathmatch.
Graphics
The graphics have not aged well. If you want good graphics wait for battlefield 5 or play battlefield 4. While the textures and weapon models look great however the terrain looks very outdated. Obviously the graphics are worse than the later games.
Sound
This is a category most people gloss over but one thing that always stood out was the excellent sound in this game. For instance when the player walks into a building and screams something it's different from when they scream it outside.
Community
Despite being released way back when dinosaurs ruled the earth back in 2010 it still has a big playerbase. It's really cool to be able to play this game and find people still playing. Other franchises, *cough* call of duty *cough*, most of the playerbase moves to the next installment and forgets the last one. This is not the case for this game.
Verdict
If you want a slightly dated but still surprisingly fun FPS game this might be a choice. However I'd recomend the later installments of the series. They have a larger playerbase, better graphics, more polish and more content.

Bottom line up front: Think a less comical Dead Rising without the stun-locking psychopathes with more than one playable character, Left4Dead-style special infected and some Walking Dead scavenging. It's no flawless diamond, but it's FUN.
Don't let the "Mixed" rating fool you. If you look up the original State of Decay (that's not longer available for purchase), you'll see it had plenty of people praising it. Most of the negative reviews for SoD seem to be original owners who were upset they bought the special edition and found it didn't offer much more than the original.
The difficulty is sneaky, and I mean that in a good way, like when you try to sneak up on a lone zombie, only to realize (too late!) that there was a cluster of zombies standing just out of sight, or when you leap out of a window to make a quick get away, only to land right in the path of a zombie horde. The tension can ramp up quick, and a moment of carelessness can result in a deadly chase.
Houses that aren't cleared every so often can get infested, leading to more freaks (special infected) and hordes wandering around (and even wind up attacking your home base). To compensate, you can build outposts, set traps and recruit more survivors to defend your home. It's a fun feature and it's nice to know you can create small pockets of (relative) safety.
My rig isn't high end by any means (Laptop, 5th Gen. Intel Core i3, integrated HD graphics), so I have to run it on minimum graphics, but it rarely chugs. Occasionally, a zombie will be standing in a wall, or I'll swing endless at a zombie and the hits won't register until I dodge away (not sure if that's a graphic problem on my end or a bug). That's about the worst problem I've encountered in my 20 hours of gameplay.
Give it a chance, especially if you can catch it on sale.

is a fascinating fighting game with great graphics and fun gameplay for those who think they would like to play a more deadly version of volleyball.
The basic objective of this game is to kick the ball away from you and kill your enemy before he manages to smash your head with a ball throw so fast it can break rocks. Basically. Although the game is initially fun, there aren't many things to discover once you figure out the basics.
First of all, I would like to point out that this game definitely looks astonishing. The visuals remind me of Party Hard, mostly because of the contrast between the dark colors and the bright neon colors. The brightest part of the screen is obviously the ring in the middle. I'm also a big fan of the effects of the game on the crowd surrounding the two players. When either one of the players or the ball is thrown out of the ring, they hit the crowd with force and leave behind a whole bunch of bodies.
The gameplay itself is quite entertaining. After I figured out the controls, I had a lot of fun playing. It takes a little while to understand the mechanics and to get used to spinning around the center all the time. You can either play against your friends locally or against the computer. The virtual opponent can be really really difficult to play against, I've only won a handful of matches against it.
Although the game is really entertaining, I realized after playing for a while that there is a surprisingly small amount of content available for the player to discover. No matter how much you play, you won't get any new skins, new skills, new arenas, nothing. There is no storyline at all to make things more interesting. I really have mixed feelings about these because I never felt bored at all, but I always had a feeling that something was missing, that there should be at least
to explore and unlock.
The soundtrack is definitely amazing, it was written by a fella called SLOTHFELLA. The music is fast-paced electronic music with a hint of futuristic sounds. I'm a big fan of it as it really fits the gameplay and especially the graphics. It's a shame there isn't a soundtrack DLC available on Steam.
Above, I talked a bit about how I needed some time to get used to the controls. At first, they are really counterintuitive, so I wish there was an option to switch the left and right key. The up and down arrows to move towards and away from the center are fine as they are quite obvious.
I'm also quite surprised that this game lacks a proper options menu. Personally, I know that Alt+Enter switches between windowed and fullscreen mode, but not a lot of people know that. If you want to change the music volume, you first have to start a game and then use the pause menu to change the volume there (and that is a really important thing to do because the music is unusually loud in this game). Another challenge for the player is to find out how to enter the pause menu at all. When I tried to do that for the first time, I was really shocked when I discovered that the Escape key doesn't do a thing is this game. Who thought this would be a good idea? After pressing a bunch of keys and giving up, I pressed Alt+F4 to close the game. Then, I reopened it and checked out the tutorial to see how to do that. Apparently, it was the P key I needed to press.
The problem with keybinds doesn't end there. The game makes absolutely no effort in explaining how to let a second player join the multiplayer game on the same keyboard. Me and my brother wanted to play on the same keyboard and we needed to press all of the most common keys to figure out which one lets the second player join. The last time we had to do that was when fifteen years ago when none of us spoke English and we couldn't understand what the instructions were saying. This time, there weren't any instructions at all.
Apart from that, there isn't much to tell about this game. It does have achievements, which is nice. I wish there was an online multiplayer mode, it would've been really neat to play this with my online friends.
Although this game suffers from of a certain amount of bad design decisions (weird keybinds, no options menu, insufficient tutorial), I found the game really enjoyable. I had a lot of time playing the game once I figured out how to actually play properly. There is certainly a lack of additional content in terms of unlockable skins, maps, game modes and other things. I think that $4 is quite an appropriate price for a game like this and I wouldn't mind them bumping it up for an additional dollar if they fixed all the flaws of this game and maybe even added the online multiplayer mode.

If you'd rather watch this review instead, click the link. Otherwise, continue below for the written review.
The core gameplay is unique, fast-paced and fun. The movement is a bit odd, you press left/right to go clockwise/counterclockwise and up/down to go out/in. You get used to it eventually, but it can be hard to use at first. You've got three different attacks based on whether you are moving in, out, or standing still. Moving in is a strong attack that makes the ball much faster, standing is a regular attack that only increases the speed slightly, and moving outwards is a stall attack that stall the ball momentarily in place before sending it back. All these add some nice depth to the game to allow for mixups and mindgames.
While the gameplay is definitely fun, what surprised me the most was how good the aesthetic is. The animations are amazing, the music is great, and the sound effects of the crowd roaring, the ball being hit, and player impacts are excellent. They all mesh with the gameplay to enhance it and make it more satisfying.
The game is local multiplayer only, and the computer player is decent to play against. Even without another person to play with I would recommend this, but WITH a friend this is a must-buy, especially at $4. No huge flaws, and some excellent gameplay and amazing aesthetic.

Let me start off by saying this was my top played Star Wars game as a child, right behind the Battlefront series. As a kid, I loved this game. The position as leader gives you the power to order your squad around, and they will willingly comply. The in-squad banter, while cheesy, made me laugh as a kid and manages to bring a smile to my face even now. I remember spending hours on the Xbox just replaying the levels and never getting bored, and even now the nostalgia still excites me and entertains me. This is not only an amazing Star Wars game, but it is also one of the greatest video games I've ever played.

Unlike a lot of people, I only thought this game was okay (I'm giving it a positive review, but only just).
I also believe that a lot of this game's positive reviews are a result of nostalgia (or being a devout Star Wars fan) at its best.
Now don't get me wrong, I'm a MASSIVE Star Wars fan, which is exactly why I'm being honest. The idea for the game was great, and parts of it are fun, but it could have been done much better. Killing Super Battle Droids was just too time consuming. Pumping clip after clip of ammo into them just got monotonous very quickly.
I did however like the conclusion of the story and thought the music was great.
The multiplayer is a different story altogether. It reminded of Halo, to an extent (especially when everyone is grabbing a rocket launcher) and had solid enough gameplay which makes it fun with a few friends.
In short, if you want a great Star Wars shooter get Battlefront II with some mods, you won't regret. I would still however pick up this game if it was on sale for the right amount since it's about as solid as any other average FPS.

I often find that people have a tendency to harp on about SW: Battlefront and KOTOR a little bit too much. They were great games, (especially the latter) but I found them to be deeply flawed games. SW: Republic Commando, while flawed in some ways, manages to pull everything together in a much more satisfying way. This is obviously due to it's genre, and the nature of the mission structure. Not a thing is out of place. This comes at price however; the mission structure is disjointed to say the least, and the story is bare bones. However you'll get the feeling this was deliberate, as just like in real combat, and especially if you're a 'slightly less expendable' clone, you'll not be kept up to the date with the war as a whole. The game will take it tacitly that you know the Star Wars lore already and fling references to the films at you without guilt or trepidation. For a avid SW fan this wont be a problem, I unfortunately found myself lost at some points in the dialogue.

The mechanics are just as you expect from a Squad shooter; intuitive, tight, and easy to control. The PC version runs great with a M&C set up, but a controller is also possible. It might be necessary to have button mapping software however, as the games age breaks the controls.
You squad mates don't need you to hold their hand, and can perform simple tasks without you needing to give the order. However, they will occasionally rush in a 'no win scenario' and be dropped in matter of seconds under a hail of plasma fire. This will happen to you over and over, and their really is no way to stop it happening. This does have the unintended use of keeping aggro off you, while you attend to other matters.
The game features the modern invent system of the FPS. That is to say. You're limited to two normal weapons, 1 special weapon, and multiple attachments to your assault rifle, thus giving the weapon variety a much needed boost. There is a weapon for every scenario.
Now, onto the soundtrack. As a avid collector of game Soundtracks, this would have a proud spot on my list. In short; it's fantastic. A mixture of choral, and star wars symphony tropes mixed together to create a chilling, but engaging and epic theme. Definitely worth getting on soundtrack.
Finally, onto the negatives, and they are surprisingly few.
The game is no looker, and is really showing it's age as of 2015. However, over a decade on and it's vista's are still rather eye catching, especially the later missions on Kashyyyk.
Also, while I said the A.I was great; that was for last decade. Now not so much. Your squad mates will get stuck on geometry and regularly fail to revive you, even if their aren't any enemies in the area. This is all forgiven however by the amazing squad dynamic of banter that is constantly being thrown around. Very rarely will you actually care what your objective is, but you'll genuinely like and care for your squad as the game progresses, and you feel like this is a family.
By no means a looker, and to modern audiences this game might feel slightly lost in why this game was so great back in the day, however I still recommend giving it a try if it comes on sale.

First off, let me just say that I am giving this a thumbs up
it is an early access game. If this was being sold simply "as is," I'd say it'd only be worth 5, maybe 6 dollars. How'd I come up with that number? If you enjoy these types of games, at a bare minimum, this game will be "new" for 2 or 3 hours, and continue to be highly enjoyable for a while after that. 5 to 6 dollars is about the same price as a movie ticket, which nets you 1-2 hours of enjoyment.
But, the game isn't being sold as is. It's being updated weekly, continually adding new content, adding to it playability, and replayability. They might add an amazing new feature, some amazing new level, or they might add something that's horrible. But that's the point. If something sucks, post about it, let SEG know. If you have an idea for something that would make the game better, let them know. You can change and steer the direction of development.
Now, the number one issue with Early Access games is devs not delivering on promises, or jumping ship with your money after a few updates. But here's the great thing about this game; although I'd be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥if the devs dropped off the face of the earth, it's already enjoyable enough that I'm willing to pay $10 for it, though not everyone is me, which is why I only gave it a "value" of 5 to 6 dollars.

First note: this is an expanded version of a free flash game available through many online game portals such as Kongregate. Given the low price and additional content and improvements in the Steam version, though, I'm not going to hold this against the game.
However, it's pretty much just another Braveland - a super short and dumbed-down King's Bounty clone. It only took me a little over an hour (69 minutes) to completely finish the Warrior's 16-stage campaign with all stars, and the Overlord's campaign was even shorter to finish, only being 6 stages long and not allowing for grinding. In general, there's not much in the way of character or army customization. Due to the unbalanced leveling rate and amount of early-game grind the game encourages as a result of it, you quickly end up with a maxed-out character, so your choices just amount to which abilities to gain first. As far as army customization, the Warrior has five army slots and six possible unit types, so your only choice is which of the unit types not to bring. In my experience, ditching the slow basic infantry unit is basically a no-brainer, so that's not even much of a choice. (And yet, it's still better than what the Mage gets, only having five unit types for five army slots. He just gets to bring everything.)
I mentioned an unbalanced leveling rate, and it's probably the only true mechanical problem this game has - it follows the King's Bounty formula of letting you recruit units up to a maximum amount defined by a Leadership score tied to your level, but until the endgame you gain levels faster than you gain money to recruit units, so any time you come close to filling up your army, you gain another level and need to spend thousands more money recruiting units. And this is if you don't need to replace lost units! In fact, replacing lost units is so expensive that early-game grind is heavily incentivized so that you can get an army strong enough to not lose any units in most of your fights.
All of the above, except for the simplicity, does not really apply to the third campaign, in which you play the final boss of the first two campaigns, however. It is far simpler than even those, as there is no level advancement or army recruitment, only you using the final boss unit and being able to summon stacks of Minions as your only spell, once per battle for each of the six battles you've previously won on any difficulty. That... does not end up having any real strategy to it at all.
In bizarre choices, by the way, this game has achievements - 14 of them, of which I have 12 - but they're not implemented through Steam, so they're only visible in-game and not on your profile. I'm not sure why they weren't implemented as Steamworks achievements.
In any case, I can't really describe Beasts Battle as a poor value, since it's $1 and probably about three hours of play, but it's also less good for anything other than a quick timewaster than even the Braveland series, which was already pretty mediocre as this subgenre goes. Stick to the actual King's Bounty games if possible, and skip Beasts Battle.
(Edit: Now I've beaten all three campaigns, though I'm missing 8 stars due to the last few Overlord levels being a bit annoying and not wanting to grind up an army for the Mage campaign's postgame levels on Normal/Hard after I lost a bunch of it.)

You are Delta 38, the leader of a group of elite clone commandos working for the republic.  You, along with your team, must do the jobs that are too big to know about and too extreme for a regular clone.  Your team is the greatest weapon you have.  Versatile, yet disfunctional, your squad consist of 07 AKA Sev, a vicious hunter who rarely ever misses, 62 AKA Scorch, the demolitions expert with the maturity of a teenager, and 40 AKA Fixer, your second-in-command and tech head who is serious, yet pure of heart.  They will either cheer for you or jeer at you.  Nevertheless, you four are family, and that's how it will always be.
PROS:
- Good characters you can invest in

- Very funny catchphrases and jeers

- Extras are interesting
CONS:
